Ka'b said: the Byzantines (al-Rum). Al-Hasan said: Persia and the Byzantines. 'Ikrimah said: Hawazin. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Hawazin and Thaqif. Qatadah said: Hawazin and Ghatafan on the day of Hunayn. Al-Zuhri and Muqatil said: Banu Hanifah, the people of al-Yamamah, the followers of Musaylimah the Liar.

Rafi' ibn Jurayj said: "By Allah, we used to recite this verse in the past: ﴿You will be called to a people of great military might﴾, and we did not know who they were until Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) called for fighting Banu Hanifah, and then we knew that they were them." Abu Hurayrah said: "This verse has not yet come (to pass)."

﴿You will fight them, or they will submit.﴾ The majority read yusalimūna (يسالمون, "they submit") in the nominative, as a conjunction with His saying "you will fight them." In the reading of Ubayy (ḥarf Ubayy) it is "aw yuslimū" (أو يسلموا), meaning "until they submit," like the saying of Imru' al-Qays: "aw yamūta fa-nu'dhara" (or he dies, so we are excused).

﴿If you obey, Allah will give you a good reward, but if you turn away, as you turned away before﴾, meaning the year of al-Hudaybiyah, ﴿He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾, which is the Fire. Ibn 'Abbas said: When this verse was revealed, the chronically ill said: "What about us, O Messenger of Allah?" So Allah the Glorious and Exalted revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾ for staying behind from jihad and sitting out the raid,

﴿nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick.﴾ (There is no blame) in that. ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and whoever turns away, He will punish him with a painful punishment.﴾ The people of Madinah and Syria read nudkhiluhu (ندخله, "We will admit him") and nu'adhdhibhu (ونعذّبه, "We will punish him") with the nūn in both places, and the rest read them with the yā' in both places. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose this, and both said: because Allah's name is mentioned before them.

﴿Allah was well pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree﴾, at al-Hudaybiyah, on condition that they would fight Quraysh and not flee.

﴿under the tree﴾ — it was a samurah tree. It is narrated that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) passed by that place after the tree had gone, and said: "Where was it?" Some of them began to say, "Here," and others, "Here." When their disagreement increased, he said: "Go on, this is excessive concern. The tree is gone; has a flood carried it away, or is it something else?"

The reason for this pledge was that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Khirash ibn Umayyah al-Khuza'i and sent him to Quraysh in Makkah, mounting him on his camel called al-Tha'lab, so that he could convey to their nobles what he had come for, at the time when he had stopped at al-Hudaybiyah. But they hamstrung the camel of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and wanted to kill him, but the al-Ahabish prevented them, and they released him, until he came to the Messenger of Allah. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) then summoned 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) to send him to Makkah. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I fear Quraysh for myself, and there is no one in Makkah from the Banu 'Adi ibn Ka'b who would protect me. Quraysh knows my enmity towards them and my harshness against them. But I will direct you to a man who is more honoured there than I am: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan." So the Messenger of Allah summoned 'Uthman and sent him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of Quraysh to inform them that he had not come for war, but had come only as a visitor to this House, to honour its sanctity. 'Uthman went out to Makkah, and Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As met him when he entered Makkah, or before he entered it. He dismounted from his mount, carried him before himself, then mounted him behind him, and escorted him until he delivered the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then the leaders of Quraysh said to 'Uthman when he had finished the message of the Messenger of Allah: "If you wish to circumambulate the House, then do so." He said: "I would not do so until the Messenger of Allah circumambulates it."

Quraysh then held him back with them. News reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims that 'Uthman had been killed. The Messenger of Allah said: "We will not leave until we fight the people." [[al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 4/191.]] He called the people to the pledge, and it was the Pledge of Ridwan (bay'at al-ridwan) under the tree. People used to say: "The Messenger of Allah took their pledge to death." Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj said: "They pledged allegiance to him to death," but the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Rather, to what you are able." [30] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/112; 'Uyun al-Athar: 2/119.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Ma'qil said: "I was standing at the head of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that day, with a branch of the samurah in my hand, warding off (flies) from him, while he took the pledge of the people. He did not take their pledge to death; rather, he took it that they would not flee."

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the pledge of the people, and no one among the Muslims who attended it stayed behind except Jadd ibn Qays, brother of Banu Salamah. It is as if I see him now, clinging to the belly of his she-camel, hiding himself from the people behind it."

The first to pledge the Pledge of Ridwan was a man from Banu Asad called Abu Sinan ibn Wahb. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came... [the narration about 'Uthman is false].

They differed about the number of those who gave the Pledge of Ridwan. Shu'bah narrated from 'Amr ibn Murrah, who said: "I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa say: 'On the day of the tree we were one thousand three hundred, and Aslam were among the Muhajirun that day.'" Qatadah said: "They were one hundred and fifteen." Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The people of the pledge under the tree were one thousand five hundred and twenty-five." Others said: "They were one thousand four hundred."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Manjawayh informed us: 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Nasrawayh narrated to us: Abu 'Imran Musa ibn Sahl ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Khawli narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "No one who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter the Fire." [31] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/350; Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/402.]]

﴿He knew what was in their hearts﴾ of sincerity, patience and fidelity. ﴿So He sent down tranquillity upon them and rewarded them with a near victory﴾, which is Khaybar, ﴿and abundant spoils they will take.﴾ Khaybar had date-palms and wealth. The Messenger of Allah divided it among them.

﴿And Allah is ever Mighty, Wise.﴾ ﴿Allah has promised you abundant spoils that you will take, and He has hastened this for you﴾, meaning the day of Khaybar. ﴿And He restrained the hands of the people from you﴾, the people of Makkah from you, through the treaty. Qatadah said: it means that He restrained the Jews of Khaybar and their allies from the tribes of Asad and Ghatafan, from your territory, your families and your property in Madinah. That was because Malik ibn 'Awf al-Nasri, 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari, and those with them from Banu Asad and Ghatafan came to support the people of Khaybar, but Allah cast terror into their hearts, and they turned back.

﴿And that it may be a sign for the believers﴾, their defeat and your safety, ﴿so that they may know that Allah is the One who protects them, guards them, in their presence and absence. ﴿And guides you to a straight path﴾: the way of trust and reliance, so that you fear God in all your affairs and rely upon Him. It was also said: He makes you firm in Islam and increases you in insight and certainty through the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah and the conquest of Khaybar.

That is because when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from the expedition of al-Hudaybiyah to Madinah, he remained there for the rest of Dhu al-Hijjah and part of Muharram, then in the latter part of Muharram of the seventh year he set out for Khaybar, and he appointed Siba' ibn 'Urfutah al-Ghifari as his deputy over Madinah.

'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Zahid informed us, reading it to him: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj informed us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us: Ibn 'Awn informed us, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Anas ibn Malik. 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj informed us: 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad Abu Yahya al-Bahili narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi 'Urwah, who said:

'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us: Rawh narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: "I was riding behind Abu Talhah on the day we came to Khaybar. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) attacked them at dawn, while they had taken their shovels and axes and gone out to their fields, and they said: 'Muhammad and the army!' The Messenger of Allah said: 'Allahu Akbar! Khaybar is ruined [[In the source: 'destroyed' instead of 'ruined'.]]. Indeed, when we descend in the courtyard [[In the source: 'in the courtyard' instead of 'courtyard'.]] of a people, evil is the morning of those who were warned.'" [32] [[Sunan al-Nasa'i: 6/132; Musnad Ahmad: 3/102.]] Then they turned back and retreated to their fortresses.

'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj narrated to us: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Hatim ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubayd, from Salamah ibn al-Akwa'.

And 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj informed us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami narrated to us: al-Nadr ibn Muhammad narrated to us: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: Salamah ibn al-Akwa' narrated to us, from his father, who said:

And it was narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Jarir, from Muhammad ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from Rahhalah, who said. And from Ibn Jarir: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: 'Awf narrated to us, from Maymun Abu 'Abd Allah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from his father, [the narrations of some of them entering into one another], they said: "We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to Khaybar, and he travelled with us at night, and 'Amir ibn al-Akwa' was with us. A man from the people said to 'Amir ibn al-Akwa': 'Will you not let us hear some of your chanting?' 'Amir was a poet, so he dismounted and began to drive the people on, reciting rajaz for them:

O Allah, were it not for You, we would not have been guided,
nor given charity, nor prayed.
Indeed, those who have rebelled against us,
and we, from Your bounty, have not been without need.
So forgive us, a ransom for You for what we have pursued,
and make our feet firm if we meet (the enemy).
And send down tranquillity upon us,
indeed, when they cry out against us, we come. [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 5/72 and 7/107; Sahih Muslim: 5/186.]]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Who is this?' They said: ''Amir ibn al-Akwa'.' He said: 'May your Lord forgive you.' A man from the people said: 'Martyrdom is due, O Prophet of Allah! If only you had let us enjoy him longer.' That is because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) never asked forgiveness for a particular man but that he was granted martyrdom. They said: 'When we arrived at Khaybar and the two sides lined up, a Jew came out, and 'Amir went out to meet him, and said:

Khaybar knows that I am 'Amir,
armed, a hero, a daring warrior. [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/52.]]

They exchanged two blows. The Jew's sword struck 'Amir's shield, and 'Amir's sword fell back upon himself, and struck his own knee and shin, and he died from it." Salamah ibn al-Akwa' said: "I passed by a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they were saying: 'The deed of 'Amir has been nullified.' So I came to the Prophet of Allah, weeping and pale, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, has the deed of 'Amir been nullified?' He said: 'Who said that?' I said: 'Some of your Companions.' He said: 'The one who said that is a liar. Rather, he has a double reward, for he truly strove and was a striver.'" [33]

Thaʿlabi said: We besieged them until severe hunger afflicted us, and then God granted us its conquest. The matter was that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave the banner to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, and those who rose with him among the people set out and met the people of Khaybar. ʿUmar and his companions were routed, so they returned to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and his companions were reproaching him and he was reproaching them. The Messenger of God had been seized by a severe headache (al-shaqiqa), so he did not come out to the people. Then Abu Bakr took the banner of the Messenger of God, rose, and fought a fierce fight, then returned. Then ʿUmar took it, fought a fierce fight, fiercer than the first fight, then returned. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was informed of that, and he said: "By God, I will surely give the banner tomorrow to a man who loves God and His Messenger, and whom God and His Messenger love; he will take it by force (ʿanwatan)." [34] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/333; Sahih al-Bukhari: 5/76; and Sahih Muslim: 7/121, with slight variation in wording.]]

ʿAli was not present. When the next day came, Abu Bakr, ʿUmar and the Quraysh stretched their necks toward it, each hoping to be the one to have it. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ to ʿAli and summoned him. ʿAli came riding a camel of his until he made it kneel near the tent of the Messenger of God. He had a severe eye inflammation, having bound his eyes with a Qatari striped cloak. Salama said: "I brought him leading him to the Prophet (ﷺ)."

The Messenger of God said: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "My eyes are inflamed." He said: "Come close to me." [35] So he drew near, and he spat into his eyes, and their pain did not return until he departed. Then he gave him the banner, and ʿAli set out with the banner, wearing a red silk garment whose fabric he had let out, and came to the city of Khaybar. Marhab, the lord of the fortress, came out wearing a saffron-dyed helmet (mighfar) and a helmet pierced like an egg on his head, saying:

"Khaybar has known that I am Marhab,
armed with weapons, a tested hero;
I strike at times and thrust at others,
when wars come upon one another with flame;
my defense is like a fire that none may approach."

ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, came out against him and said:

"I am the one whom my mother named Haydara,
like a lion of thickets, fierce and mighty of aspect;
I measure out to you with the sword the measure of the sandara."

They exchanged two blows, but ʿAli got the better of him, struck him, split the helmet and the head, and the sword reached the molars. He took the city, and the conquest was at his hands. Then after Marhab came out his brother Yasir ibn Nahr, saying:

"Khaybar has known that I am Yasir,
armed with weapons, a hero of raids;
when lions come rushing forward,
and the raiders hold back from my assault,
my defense in it is present death."

He kept saying: "Is there anyone to duel?" So al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam came out to him, saying:

"Khaybar has known that I am Zabbar,
a noble one against a noble, not one who turns back in flight,
son of the glory of the honored, son of the good,
Yasir, let the host of the unbelievers not deceive you,
and their multitude is like the scattering mirage."

His mother Safiyya bint ʿAbd al-Muttalib said: "Will my son be killed, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Rather, your son will kill him, God willing." Then they met, and al-Zubayr killed him. Abu Rafiʿ, the freedman of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), said: "We went out with ʿAli ibn Abi Talib when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent him with his banner. When he approached the fortress, its people came out to him and fought them, and a man of the Jews struck him, so his shield fell from his hand. ʿAli took a door that was at the fortress and used it as a shield to protect himself, and it stayed in his hand while he fought until God granted him victory. Then he threw it from his hand when he finished. I saw myself with a group of seven, I being the eighth, struggling to turn that door over, but we could not turn it." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/301.]]

Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) continued to conquer the fortresses one by one and to divide the wealth, until they reached the fortress of al-Watih and al-Salalim, which was the last of the fortresses of Khaybar to be conquered. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) besieged them for some dozen nights. When the people had evening on the day of the conquest, they lit many fires, and the Messenger of God said: "For what are you lighting these?" They said: "For meat." He said: "What meat?" They said: "The meat of domestic donkeys." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Pour it out and break it." A man said: "Or shall we pour it out and wash it?" He said: "Or that." [36] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 3/107.]]

Ibn Ishaq said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) conquered al-Qamus, the fortress of the Banu Abi al-Huqayq, Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab was brought to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), along with another woman with her. Bilal passed by them—he was the one who had brought them past the corpses of the Jewish men who had been killed. When the other woman with Safiyya saw them, she shrieked, struck her face, and threw dust on her head. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw her, he said: "Take this she-devil away from me!" He ordered that Safiyya be taken, and she walked behind him, and he threw his cloak over her, and the Muslims knew that the Messenger of God had chosen her for himself.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Bilal, when he saw what he had done to that Jewish woman: "Has mercy been removed from you, O Bilal, that you pass by two women over the corpses of their men?" Safiyya had seen in a dream, while she was a bride of Kinana ibn al-Rabiʿ ibn Abi al-Huqayq, that a moon had fallen into her lap. She related her vision to her husband, and he said: "This is nothing but that you long for the king of the Hijaz, Muhammad." He slapped her face, and her eye turned green from it. She came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) with the mark of it still on her.

He asked her: "What is it?" She told him this report. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) brought her husband Kinana ibn al-Rabiʿ ibn Abi al-Huqayq, who had the treasure of the Banu al-Nadir. He questioned him, and he denied knowing its location. A man of the Jews was brought to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "I have seen Kinana going around this vault every morning." The Messenger of God said to Kinana: "Do you see, if we find it with you, I will kill you?" He said: "Yes."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) ordered the vault to be dug up, and some of their treasure was taken out of it. Then he asked him about what remained, but he refused to hand it over. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) commanded al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam regarding him, and said: "Torture him until you extract what he has." [37] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/302; al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/224.]]

Al-Zubayr began striking his chest with a firebrand until he came close to death. Then the Messenger of God handed him over to Muhammad ibn Maslama, who struck his neck, avenging his brother Mahmud ibn Maslama, whom the Jews had struck with a stone near the fortress of Na'im, and killed him. It was the first fortress of Khaybar to be conquered.

They said: When the people of Fadak heard what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had done at Khaybar, they sent to the Messenger of God asking him to spare them, to preserve their blood for them, and to leave the wealth to him. He did so. Then the people of Khaybar asked the Messenger of God to deal with them over the wealth for half the produce, and he agreed to that, on the condition that "if we wish, we may expel you." The people of Fadak made a similar arrangement with him. Khaybar was spoils (fay') for the Muslims, while Fadak was exclusively for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), for they had not advanced against it with horse or camel: "for you did not press forward against it with horse or riding-camel."

When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was at ease, Zaynab bint al-Harith, the wife of Sallam ibn Mishkam, presented him with a roasted sheep. She had asked which part of the sheep was most beloved to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she was told: the foreleg. So she put a great deal of poison into it, and poisoned the rest of the sheep. Then she brought it, and when she placed it before the Messenger of God, he took the foreleg and bit off a morsel from it, but did not swallow it. With him was Bishr ibn al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, who had taken from it as the Messenger of God had taken. Bishr swallowed it, but the Messenger of God spat it out. Then he said: "This bone is telling me that it is poisoned." He summoned her, and she confessed. He said: "What moved you to do that?" She said: "I have suffered from my people what is not hidden from you. I said: If he is a prophet, he will be informed; and if he is a king, I will be rid of him." He said:

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) pardoned her, and Bishr ibn al-Bara' died from the morsel he had eaten.

He said: Umm Bishr, the mother of Bishr ibn al-Bara', came to visit the Messenger of God (ﷺ) during his illness in which he died. He said: "O Umm Bishr, the morsel of Khaybar that I ate at Khaybar with your son has never ceased to trouble me; now is the time for the cutting of my aorta." [38] [[al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/240.]]

The Muslims used to hold that the Messenger of God died as a martyr, in addition to the prophethood with which God had honored him.

"And another [victory] which you have not been able to achieve, God has already encompassed it" — i.e., the promise of conquering another city, until He grants it to you. Ibn ʿAbbas said: God knew that He would give it to you. They differed about it: Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, al-Hasan and Muqatil said: it is Persia and Byzantium.

al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd and Ibn Ishaq said: it is Khaybar; God promised it to His Prophet before he attained it, and they had neither mentioned it nor hoped for it until God informed them of it. This is also the narration of ʿAtiyya and Mazadhan from Ibn ʿAbbas. Qatada said: it is Mecca. ʿIkrima said: it is Khaybar. Mujahid said: it is what they had not conquered until today. "And God is over all things competent."

Al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 48, verses 10–21 (part 1 of 2)

﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, O Muhammad, at al-Hudaybiyah, on condition that they will not flee, they are only pledging allegiance to Allah.﴾

Ibn Manjawayh informed us: Ibn Habash al-Muqri narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Imran narrated to us: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Makhzumi narrated to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, that he heard Jabir say: "On the day of al-Hudaybiyah we were one thousand four hundred. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: 'You are today the best people on earth.'" [29] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 5/63; Sahih Muslim: 6/26.]] He said: Jabir also said to us: "If I could see, I would show you the place of the tree." And he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took our pledge beneath the samurah tree, to death, that we would not flee. None of us broke the pledge, except Jadd ibn Qays, who was a hypocrite. He hid under the belly of his camel and did not march with the people."

﴿The hand of Allah is over their hands.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "The hand of Allah" refers to fulfilling what He promised them of good, "over their hands" refers to fulfilling (the pledge).

Al-Suddi said: "The hand of Allah is over their hands" — this is because they used to take hold of the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and pledge allegiance to him, and "the hand of Allah is over their hands" at the time of the pledge.

Al-Kalbi said: its meaning is the blessing of Allah upon them, which is above what they did in the pledge. Ibn Kaysan said: the power of Allah and His support are above their power and support.

﴿So whoever breaks (the pledge)﴾, meaning the pledge, ﴿only breaks it to his own detriment﴾, its harm falls upon him. ﴿And whoever fulfills what he has covenanted with Allah, He will give him﴾ — the people of Iraq read it with the yā’ (ﯾ, "He will give") and the others with the nūn (ʼ, "We will give").

﴿a great reward﴾, which is Paradise.

﴿Those who were left behind of the Bedouins will say to you﴾

Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: they mean the Bedouin tribes of Ghifar, Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Ashja', Aslam, and al-Dil. That was because when the Prophet (ﷺ) intended to set out for Makkah in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, to perform 'umrah, he called upon the Bedouins and the desert dwellers around Madinah to go out with him, fearing that Quraysh might confront him in battle and prevent him from the House. He himself entered the state of ihram and took with him the sacrificial animals, so that people would know that he did not intend war. But many of the Bedouins held back from him and said: "We will go with him to a people who came to him, killed his companions, and we will fight them," so they stayed behind. They gave the excuse of being occupied.

Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Those who were left behind of the Bedouins will say to you﴾, those whom Allah left behind from accompanying you and serving you on your pilgrimage and your 'umrah, when you return to them, so you rebuked them for staying behind from you.

﴿Our wealth and our families kept us busy, so ask forgiveness for us﴾. Then He denied them in their excuse and their request for forgiveness, and informed of their hidden intentions and concealed thoughts, saying: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say: "Who then can avail you anything against Allah, if He intends harm for you, or intends benefit for you?"﴾ Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read ḍarran (ضرًّا, "harm") with a ḍammah on the ḍād, and the rest read it with a fatḥah. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose this reading, and both said: because He set it against benefit, the opposite of harm.

﴿Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do.﴾ ﴿Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and that was made attractive in your hearts, and you harboured an evil assumption; and you were a people ruined.﴾ That is because they said: "Muhammad and his companions are a mouthful for the enemy (akalat ra's, lit. 'people who will be devoured'), so they will not return. Where are you going? Wait and see what becomes of their affair." ﴿And you were a people ruined﴾: lost, corrupt, unfit for anything good.

﴿And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger — indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a blazing fire.﴾ ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

﴿Those who were left behind will say, when you set out to take spoils﴾, meaning the spoils of Khaybar, ﴿"Leave us, that we may follow you."﴾ That is, to Khaybar, so that we may witness with you. ﴿They want to change the word of Allah.﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "kalam Allah" (كلم الله) without the alif, and the rest read "kalam Allah" (كَلامَ اللَّهِ). Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose this. Al-Farra' said: al-kalam is a verbal noun, and al-kalim is the plural of kalimah. The meaning of the verse is: they want to alter the promise of Allah that He made to the people of al-Hudaybiyah, since Allah made the spoils of Khaybar theirs as a substitute for the spoils of Makkah, if they withdrew from them by treaty and did not gain anything from them. Ibn Zayd said: it refers to His saying: ﴿So if they seek your permission to go out, say: "You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me."﴾ [[Surat al-Tawbah: 83.]] But the first opinion is more correct and closer to the truth, because the majority of the people of ta'wil (interpretation) hold it, and it better matches the apparent sense of the revelation (tanzil), since His saying ﴿"You will never go out with me, ever"﴾ was revealed concerning the expedition of Tabuk.

﴿Say: "You will never follow us; thus has Allah said before﴾, that is, before our return to you: that the spoils of Khaybar are for those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyah, and no one else has a share in them.

﴿They will say: "Rather, you envy us."﴾ That is, that we might gain a share of the spoils with you. ﴿Rather, they did not understand except a little.﴾

﴿Say to those left behind of the Bedouins: "You will be called to a people of great military might; you will fight them or they will submit."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, and Mujahid said: they are Persia. Ka'b said: the Byzantines (al-Rum). Al-Hasan said: Persia and the Byzantines. 'Ikrimah said: Hawazin. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Hawazin and Thaqif. Qatadah said: Hawazin and Ghatafan on the day of Hunayn. Al-Zuhri and Muqatil said: Banu Hanifah, the people of al-Yamamah, the followers of Musaylimah the Liar.

Rafi' ibn Jurayj said: "By Allah, we used to recite this verse in the past: ﴿You will be called to a people of great military might﴾, and we did not know who they were until Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) called for fighting Banu Hanifah, and then we knew that they were them." Abu Hurayrah said: "This verse has not yet come (to pass)."

﴿You will fight them, or they will submit.﴾ The majority read yusalimūna (يسالمون, "they submit") in the nominative, as a conjunction with His saying "you will fight them." In the reading of Ubayy (ḥarf Ubayy) it is "aw yuslimū" (أو يسلموا), meaning "until they submit," like the saying of Imru' al-Qays: "aw yamūta fa-nu'dhara" (or he dies, so we are excused).

﴿If you obey, Allah will give you a good reward, but if you turn away, as you turned away before﴾, meaning the year of al-Hudaybiyah, ﴿He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾, which is the Fire. Ibn 'Abbas said: When this verse was revealed, the chronically ill said: "What about us, O Messenger of Allah?" So Allah the Glorious and Exalted revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾ for staying behind from jihad and sitting out the raid,

﴿nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick.﴾ (There is no blame) in that. ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and whoever turns away, He will punish him with a painful punishment.﴾ The people of Madinah and Syria read nudkhiluhu (ندخله, "We will admit him") and nu'adhdhibhu (ونعذّبه, "We will punish him") with the nūn in both places, and the rest read them with the yā' in both places. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose this, and both said: because Allah's name is mentioned before them.

﴿Allah was well pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree﴾, at al-Hudaybiyah, on condition that they would fight Quraysh and not flee.

﴿under the tree﴾ — it was a samurah tree. It is narrated that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) passed by that place after the tree had gone, and said: "Where was it?" Some of them began to say, "Here," and others, "Here." When their disagreement increased, he said: "Go on, this is excessive concern. The tree is gone; has a flood carried it away, or is it something else?"

The reason for this pledge was that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Khirash ibn Umayyah al-Khuza'i and sent him to Quraysh in Makkah, mounting him on his camel called al-Tha'lab, so that he could convey to their nobles what he had come for, at the time when he had stopped at al-Hudaybiyah. But they hamstrung the camel of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and wanted to kill him, but the al-Ahabish prevented them, and they released him, until he came to the Messenger of Allah. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) then summoned 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) to send him to Makkah. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I fear Quraysh for myself, and there is no one in Makkah from the Banu 'Adi ibn Ka'b who would protect me. Quraysh knows my enmity towards them and my harshness against them. But I will direct you to a man who is more honoured there than I am: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan." So the Messenger of Allah summoned 'Uthman and sent him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of Quraysh to inform them that he had not come for war, but had come only as a visitor to this House, to honour its sanctity. 'Uthman went out to Makkah, and Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As met him when he entered Makkah, or before he entered it. He dismounted from his mount, carried him before himself, then mounted him behind him, and escorted him until he delivered the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then the leaders of Quraysh said to 'Uthman when he had finished the message of the Messenger of Allah: "If you wish to circumambulate the House, then do so." He said: "I would not do so until the Messenger of Allah circumambulates it."

Quraysh then held him back with them. News reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims that 'Uthman had been killed. The Messenger of Allah said: "We will not leave until we fight the people." [[al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 4/191.]] He called the people to the pledge, and it was the Pledge of Ridwan (bay'at al-ridwan) under the tree. People used to say: "The Messenger of Allah took their pledge to death." Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj said: "They pledged allegiance to him to death," but the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Rather, to what you are able." [30] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/112; 'Uyun al-Athar: 2/119.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Ma'qil said: "I was standing at the head of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that day, with a branch of the samurah in my hand, warding off (flies) from him, while he took the pledge of the people. He did not take their pledge to death; rather, he took it that they would not flee."

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the pledge of the people, and no one among the Muslims who attended it stayed behind except Jadd ibn Qays, brother of Banu Salamah. It is as if I see him now, clinging to the belly of his she-camel, hiding himself from the people behind it."

The first to pledge the Pledge of Ridwan was a man from Banu Asad called Abu Sinan ibn Wahb. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came... [the narration about 'Uthman is false].

They differed about the number of those who gave the Pledge of Ridwan. Shu'bah narrated from 'Amr ibn Murrah, who said: "I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa say: 'On the day of the tree we were one thousand three hundred, and Aslam were among the Muhajirun that day.'" Qatadah said: "They were one hundred and fifteen." Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The people of the pledge under the tree were one thousand five hundred and twenty-five." Others said: "They were one thousand four hundred."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Manjawayh informed us: 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Nasrawayh narrated to us: Abu 'Imran Musa ibn Sahl ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Khawli narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "No one who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter the Fire." [31] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/350; Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/402.]]

﴿He knew what was in their hearts﴾ of sincerity, patience and fidelity. ﴿So He sent down tranquillity upon them and rewarded them with a near victory﴾, which is Khaybar, ﴿and abundant spoils they will take.﴾ Khaybar had date-palms and wealth. The Messenger of Allah divided it among them.

﴿And Allah is ever Mighty, Wise.﴾ ﴿Allah has promised you abundant spoils that you will take, and He has hastened this for you﴾, meaning the day of Khaybar. ﴿And He restrained the hands of the people from you﴾, the people of Makkah from you, through the treaty. Qatadah said: it means that He restrained the Jews of Khaybar and their allies from the tribes of Asad and Ghatafan, from your territory, your families and your property in Madinah. That was because Malik ibn 'Awf al-Nasri, 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari, and those with them from Banu Asad and Ghatafan came to support the people of Khaybar, but Allah cast terror into their hearts, and they turned back.

﴿And that it may be a sign for the believers﴾, their defeat and your safety, ﴿so that they may know that Allah is the One who protects them, guards them, in their presence and absence. ﴿And guides you to a straight path﴾: the way of trust and reliance, so that you fear God in all your affairs and rely upon Him. It was also said: He makes you firm in Islam and increases you in insight and certainty through the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah and the conquest of Khaybar.

That is because when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from the expedition of al-Hudaybiyah to Madinah, he remained there for the rest of Dhu al-Hijjah and part of Muharram, then in the latter part of Muharram of the seventh year he set out for Khaybar, and he appointed Siba' ibn 'Urfutah al-Ghifari as his deputy over Madinah.

'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Zahid informed us, reading it to him: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj informed us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us: Ibn 'Awn informed us, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Anas ibn Malik. 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj informed us: 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad Abu Yahya al-Bahili narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi 'Urwah, who said:

'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us: Rawh narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: "I was riding behind Abu Talhah on the day we came to Khaybar. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) attacked them at dawn, while they had taken their shovels and axes and gone out to their fields, and they said: 'Muhammad and the army!' The Messenger of Allah said: 'Allahu Akbar! Khaybar is ruined [[In the source: 'destroyed' instead of 'ruined'.]]. Indeed, when we descend in the courtyard [[In the source: 'in the courtyard' instead of 'courtyard'.]] of a people, evil is the morning of those who were warned.'" [32] [[Sunan al-Nasa'i: 6/132; Musnad Ahmad: 3/102.]] Then they turned back and retreated to their fortresses.

'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj narrated to us: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Hatim ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubayd, from Salamah ibn al-Akwa'.

And 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj informed us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami narrated to us: al-Nadr ibn Muhammad narrated to us: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: Salamah ibn al-Akwa' narrated to us, from his father, who said:

And it was narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Jarir, from Muhammad ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from Rahhalah, who said. And from Ibn Jarir: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: 'Awf narrated to us, from Maymun Abu 'Abd Allah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from his father, [the narrations of some of them entering into one another], they said: "We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to Khaybar, and he travelled with us at night, and 'Amir ibn al-Akwa' was with us. A man from the people said to 'Amir ibn al-Akwa': 'Will you not let us hear some of your chanting?' 'Amir was a poet, so he dismounted and began to drive the people on, reciting rajaz for them:

O Allah, were it not for You, we would not have been guided,
nor given charity, nor prayed.
Indeed, those who have rebelled against us,
and we, from Your bounty, have not been without need.
So forgive us, a ransom for You for what we have pursued,
and make our feet firm if we meet (the enemy).
And send down tranquillity upon us,
indeed, when they cry out against us, we come. [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 5/72 and 7/107; Sahih Muslim: 5/186.]]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Who is this?' They said: ''Amir ibn al-Akwa'.' He said: 'May your Lord forgive you.' A man from the people said: 'Martyrdom is due, O Prophet of Allah! If only you had let us enjoy him longer.' That is because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) never asked forgiveness for a particular man but that he was granted martyrdom. They said: 'When we arrived at Khaybar and the two sides lined up, a Jew came out, and 'Amir went out to meet him, and said:

Khaybar knows that I am 'Amir,
armed, a hero, a daring warrior. [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/52.]]

They exchanged two blows. The Jew's sword struck 'Amir's shield, and 'Amir's sword fell back upon himself, and struck his own knee and shin, and he died from it." Salamah ibn al-Akwa' said: "I passed by a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they were saying: 'The deed of 'Amir has been nullified.' So I came to the Prophet of Allah, weeping and pale, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, has the deed of 'Amir been nullified?' He said: 'Who said that?' I said: 'Some of your Companions.' He said: 'The one who said that is a liar. Rather, he has a double reward, for he truly strove and was a striver.'" [33]

Thaʿlabi said: We besieged them until severe hunger afflicted us, and then God granted us its conquest. The matter was that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave the banner to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, and those who rose with him among the people set out and met the people of Khaybar. ʿUmar and his companions were routed, so they returned to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and his companions were reproaching him and he was reproaching them. The Messenger of God had been seized by a severe headache (al-shaqiqa), so he did not come out to the people. Then Abu Bakr took the banner of the Messenger of God, rose, and fought a fierce fight, then returned. Then ʿUmar took it, fought a fierce fight, fiercer than the first fight, then returned. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was informed of that, and he said: "By God, I will surely give the banner tomorrow to a man who loves God and His Messenger, and whom God and His Messenger love; he will take it by force (ʿanwatan)." [34] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/333; Sahih al-Bukhari: 5/76; and Sahih Muslim: 7/121, with slight variation in wording.]]

ʿAli was not present. When the next day came, Abu Bakr, ʿUmar and the Quraysh stretched their necks toward it, each hoping to be the one to have it. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ to ʿAli and summoned him. ʿAli came riding a camel of his until he made it kneel near the tent of the Messenger of God. He had a severe eye inflammation, having bound his eyes with a Qatari striped cloak. Salama said: "I brought him leading him to the Prophet (ﷺ)."

The Messenger of God said: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "My eyes are inflamed." He said: "Come close to me." [35] So he drew near, and he spat into his eyes, and their pain did not return until he departed. Then he gave him the banner, and ʿAli set out with the banner, wearing a red silk garment whose fabric he had let out, and came to the city of Khaybar. Marhab, the lord of the fortress, came out wearing a saffron-dyed helmet (mighfar) and a helmet pierced like an egg on his head, saying:

"Khaybar has known that I am Marhab,
armed with weapons, a tested hero;
I strike at times and thrust at others,
when wars come upon one another with flame;
my defense is like a fire that none may approach."

ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, came out against him and said:

"I am the one whom my mother named Haydara,
like a lion of thickets, fierce and mighty of aspect;
I measure out to you with the sword the measure of the sandara."

They exchanged two blows, but ʿAli got the better of him, struck him, split the helmet and the head, and the sword reached the molars. He took the city, and the conquest was at his hands. Then after Marhab came out his brother Yasir ibn Nahr, saying:

"Khaybar has known that I am Yasir,
armed with weapons, a hero of raids;
when lions come rushing forward,
and the raiders hold back from my assault,
my defense in it is present death."

He kept saying: "Is there anyone to duel?" So al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam came out to him, saying:

"Khaybar has known that I am Zabbar,
a noble one against a noble, not one who turns back in flight,
son of the glory of the honored, son of the good,
Yasir, let the host of the unbelievers not deceive you,
and their multitude is like the scattering mirage."

His mother Safiyya bint ʿAbd al-Muttalib said: "Will my son be killed, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Rather, your son will kill him, God willing." Then they met, and al-Zubayr killed him. Abu Rafiʿ, the freedman of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), said: "We went out with ʿAli ibn Abi Talib when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent him with his banner. When he approached the fortress, its people came out to him and fought them, and a man of the Jews struck him, so his shield fell from his hand. ʿAli took a door that was at the fortress and used it as a shield to protect himself, and it stayed in his hand while he fought until God granted him victory. Then he threw it from his hand when he finished. I saw myself with a group of seven, I being the eighth, struggling to turn that door over, but we could not turn it." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/301.]]

Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) continued to conquer the fortresses one by one and to divide the wealth, until they reached the fortress of al-Watih and al-Salalim, which was the last of the fortresses of Khaybar to be conquered. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) besieged them for some dozen nights. When the people had evening on the day of the conquest, they lit many fires, and the Messenger of God said: "For what are you lighting these?" They said: "For meat." He said: "What meat?" They said: "The meat of domestic donkeys." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Pour it out and break it." A man said: "Or shall we pour it out and wash it?" He said: "Or that." [36] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 3/107.]]

Ibn Ishaq said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) conquered al-Qamus, the fortress of the Banu Abi al-Huqayq, Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab was brought to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), along with another woman with her. Bilal passed by them—he was the one who had brought them past the corpses of the Jewish men who had been killed. When the other woman with Safiyya saw them, she shrieked, struck her face, and threw dust on her head. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw her, he said: "Take this she-devil away from me!" He ordered that Safiyya be taken, and she walked behind him, and he threw his cloak over her, and the Muslims knew that the Messenger of God had chosen her for himself.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Bilal, when he saw what he had done to that Jewish woman: "Has mercy been removed from you, O Bilal, that you pass by two women over the corpses of their men?" Safiyya had seen in a dream, while she was a bride of Kinana ibn al-Rabiʿ ibn Abi al-Huqayq, that a moon had fallen into her lap. She related her vision to her husband, and he said: "This is nothing but that you long for the king of the Hijaz, Muhammad." He slapped her face, and her eye turned green from it. She came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) with the mark of it still on her.

He asked her: "What is it?" She told him this report. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) brought her husband Kinana ibn al-Rabiʿ ibn Abi al-Huqayq, who had the treasure of the Banu al-Nadir. He questioned him, and he denied knowing its location. A man of the Jews was brought to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "I have seen Kinana going around this vault every morning." The Messenger of God said to Kinana: "Do you see, if we find it with you, I will kill you?" He said: "Yes."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) ordered the vault to be dug up, and some of their treasure was taken out of it. Then he asked him about what remained, but he refused to hand it over. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) commanded al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam regarding him, and said: "Torture him until you extract what he has." [37] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/302; al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/224.]]

Al-Zubayr began striking his chest with a firebrand until he came close to death. Then the Messenger of God handed him over to Muhammad ibn Maslama, who struck his neck, avenging his brother Mahmud ibn Maslama, whom the Jews had struck with a stone near the fortress of Na'im, and killed him. It was the first fortress of Khaybar to be conquered.

They said: When the people of Fadak heard what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had done at Khaybar, they sent to the Messenger of God asking him to spare them, to preserve their blood for them, and to leave the wealth to him. He did so. Then the people of Khaybar asked the Messenger of God to deal with them over the wealth for half the produce, and he agreed to that, on the condition that "if we wish, we may expel you." The people of Fadak made a similar arrangement with him. Khaybar was spoils (fay') for the Muslims, while Fadak was exclusively for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), for they had not advanced against it with horse or camel: "for you did not press forward against it with horse or riding-camel."

When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was at ease, Zaynab bint al-Harith, the wife of Sallam ibn Mishkam, presented him with a roasted sheep. She had asked which part of the sheep was most beloved to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she was told: the foreleg. So she put a great deal of poison into it, and poisoned the rest of the sheep. Then she brought it, and when she placed it before the Messenger of God, he took the foreleg and bit off a morsel from it, but did not swallow it. With him was Bishr ibn al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, who had taken from it as the Messenger of God had taken. Bishr swallowed it, but the Messenger of God spat it out. Then he said: "This bone is telling me that it is poisoned." He summoned her, and she confessed. He said: "What moved you to do that?" She said: "I have suffered from my people what is not hidden from you. I said: If he is a prophet, he will be informed; and if he is a king, I will be rid of him." He said:

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) pardoned her, and Bishr ibn al-Bara' died from the morsel he had eaten.

He said: Umm Bishr, the mother of Bishr ibn al-Bara', came to visit the Messenger of God (ﷺ) during his illness in which he died. He said: "O Umm Bishr, the morsel of Khaybar that I ate at Khaybar with your son has never ceased to trouble me; now is the time for the cutting of my aorta." [38] [[al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/240.]]

The Muslims used to hold that the Messenger of God died as a martyr, in addition to the prophethood with which God had honored him.

"And another [victory] which you have not been able to achieve, God has already encompassed it" — i.e., the promise of conquering another city, until He grants it to you. Ibn ʿAbbas said: God knew that He would give it to you. They differed about it: Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, al-Hasan and Muqatil said: it is Persia and Byzantium.

al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd and Ibn Ishaq said: it is Khaybar; God promised it to His Prophet before he attained it, and they had neither mentioned it nor hoped for it until God informed them of it. This is also the narration of ʿAtiyya and Mazadhan from Ibn ʿAbbas. Qatada said: it is Mecca. ʿIkrima said: it is Khaybar. Mujahid said: it is what they had not conquered until today. "And God is over all things competent."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (*al-Jawahir al-Hisan*) on surah 48, verses 22–27 (part 1 of 3):

﴿And if those who disbelieve fought you, they would surely turn their backs; then they would find neither a protector nor a helper.﴾ He means Asad, Ghatafan, and the people of Khaybar. Qatadah said: He means the disbelievers of Quraysh. ﴿The way of Allah, which has already passed before, and you will not find any change in the way of Allah.﴾ That is, like the way of Allah which has passed before, in granting victory to His friends and subduing His enemies. ﴿And He is the One who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the heart of Mecca,﴾ that is, al-Hudaybiyyah, ﴿after He had given you victory over them. And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do.﴾ (*al-Ya'*) Abu 'Amr and others read it with *ya'* (they), and others read it with *ta'* (you). They differed concerning who they were. Anas said: Eighty men from the people of Mecca descended upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions from the mountain of al-Tan'im at the time of the dawn prayer during the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, intending to kill them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took them alive and set them free. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And He is the One who withheld their hands from you…﴾ to the end of the verse.

'Ikrimah related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Quraysh had sent forty or fifty men from among them, and ordered them to circle around the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, to strike some of his companions, but they were seized. They were brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he pardoned them and released them. They had been pelting the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with stones and arrows. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And He is the One who withheld their hands from you…﴾ to the end of the verse.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughaffal said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) at al-Hudaybiyyah, beneath the root of a tree, and a branch of that tree was on his back. I lifted it from his back. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib was before him writing the treaty of peace, and Suhayl ibn 'Amr was there. Thirty young men came out to us armed, and they rushed at us. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) invoked Allah, and Allah blinded their sight. We stood up to them, seized them, and the Messenger of Allah released them. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse. [39] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/281.]]

Mujahid said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) came out intending to perform 'umrah, and his companions seized some people from the sanctuary who were unaware. The Prophet (ﷺ) released them. That is the "victory" in ﴿the heart of Mecca﴾.

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that a man among the companions of the Messenger of Allah, called Zunaym, looked out from the pass of al-Hudaybiyyah. The polytheists shot him with an arrow and killed him. The Messenger of Allah sent cavalry, and they brought twelve disbelieving horsemen. The Prophet of Allah said to them: "Do you have a covenant with me? Do you have a pact with me?" [40] They said: No. So he released them, and Allah revealed this verse.

Ibn Ayzi and al-Kalbi said: They were the people of al-Hudaybiyyah. When the Prophet (ﷺ) set out with the sacrificial animals and reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: "O Prophet of Allah, will you enter upon a people who are at war with you without weapons or horses?" He sent to Medina, and he left no horse or weapon there without taking it. When he approached Mecca, they prevented him from entering. He went on until he came to Mina, and he stayed at Mina. Then a spy came to him saying that 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl had come out against you with five hundred men. He said to Khalid ibn al-Walid: "O Khalid, this is your cousin who has come to you with horses." Khalid said: "I am the sword of Allah and the sword of His Messenger, O Messenger of Allah, send me wherever you wish." On that day he was named "the Sword of Allah." He sent him with cavalry, and he met 'Ikrimah in the ravine and defeated him until he drove him into the walls of Mecca. Then they returned a second time, and he defeated him until he drove him into the walls of Mecca. Then he returned a third time, and he defeated him until he drove him into the walls of Mecca. So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And He is the One who withheld their hands from you…﴾ to His saying ﴿a painful punishment﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) withheld from the remnants of the Muslims who had remained there after He had granted him victory over them, out of aversion that the horses might trample them without knowledge. [41] This is His saying: ﴿They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and the sacrificial animals detained from reaching their place of sacrifice.﴾ That is, they barred the sacrificial animals, held back. [42] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/123.]]

﴿from reaching their place of sacrifice﴾, that is, their place of slaughter. They were seventy camels.

Al-Zuhri related, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who both said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) left Medina in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, intending to visit the House, not intending fighting. He took with him seventy camels, and the people were seven hundred men, so each camel was for ten persons. When he reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, people joined him, and he set out with some hundreds of his companions. When they were at Dhu al-Hulayfah, he garlanded the sacrificial animals, marked them, and entered into the state of ihram for 'umrah. He sent ahead a spy from Khuza'ah to inform him about Quraysh.

The Prophet (ﷺ) continued until, when he was at the pool of al-Ashtat, near 'Usfan, the Khuza'i spy came to him and said: "I left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy and 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, who have gathered the Ahabish for you. They will fight you and bar you from the House." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Advise me. Do you think we should attack the offspring of those who assisted them and take them captive? If they remain seated, they will sit as men who have been wronged, and if they escape, it will be a neck which Allah has cut off. Or do you think we should head for the House, and whoever bars us from it, we will fight him?"

Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have not come to fight anyone, but whoever stands between us and the House, we will fight him." The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Then set out."

Abu Hurayrah used to say: I never saw anyone more consultative with his companions than the Prophet (ﷺ). They set out until, when they were at 'Usfan, Bishr ibn Sufyan al-Ka'bi met him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, these are Quraysh. They have heard of your journey, so they have come out with their nursing camels and their suckling young, wearing leopard skins. They have camped at Dhu Tuwa, swearing by Allah that you will never enter upon them. And this is Khalid ibn al-Walid with their horses, who have advanced them to Kura' al-Ghamim." I have mentioned the saying of one who said: On that day Khalid ibn al-Walid was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as a Muslim. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Woe to Quraysh! War has consumed them. What harm would it do them if they left me between myself and the rest of the Arabs? If they overcome me, that is what they wanted, and if Allah makes me victorious over them, they will enter Islam in multitudes, and if they do not do that, they will fight while still possessing strength. What does Quraysh think? By Allah, I will not cease to strive against them for the sake of what Allah has sent me with, until Allah makes it prevail, or my neck is severed." [43] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/323; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 20/16.]]

Then he said: "Who will lead us by a route other than the one they are on?" A man from Aslam said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." So he led them on a rough, difficult path between ravines. When they came out of it, the Muslims had found that burdensome, and it led to a level land at the end of the valley. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the people: "Say: We seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him." They did so, and he said: "By Allah, this is the 'hittah' (remission) that was presented to the Children of Israel, but they did not say it." [44] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/273; al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 4/189.]]

Then the Messenger of Allah said to the people: "Take the route to the right," along a path that leads out at the pass of al-Murar, descending upon al-Hudaybiyyah from the lower part of Mecca.

The army took that route. When the horsemen of Quraysh saw the departure of Quraysh (from its own route) and that the Messenger of Allah had diverged from their path, they spurred back to Quraysh to warn them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued until, when he took the pass of al-Murar, his she-camel knelt down with him. The people said: "Hal, hal!" He said: "What is 'hal'?" They said: "She has been made to stop, by force." He said: "She has not been made to stop, and that is not her habit, but the one who stopped the elephant has stopped her." [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/323; Sahih al-Bukhari: 3/178 with variation; Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/629.]] [45]

Then he said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, Quraysh will not ask me today for any arrangement by which they glorify the sacred things of Allah, and in which there is the maintenance of kinship, except that I will give it to them." Then he said to the people: "Dismount." They dismounted at the farthest part of al-Hudaybiyyah, at a well of little water, from which people could only take water in small amounts. The people soon exhausted it. The people complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of thirst. He drew an arrow from his quiver and gave it to a man of his companions called Najiyah ibn 'Umayr ibn Ya'mur ibn Darim, who was the driver of the sacrificial camels of the Messenger of Allah. He descended into that well and thrust it into its bottom, and the water gushed forth with abundance, until they departed from it. It is said that a girl from the Ansar came with her bucket, while Najiyah was in the well drawing water for the people, and she said:

"O you who draw water, my bucket is yours,
for I see the people praising you,
extolling your goodness and glorifying you;
I hope for good from you as they hope from you."

He said:

"The Yemeni girl knows
that I am the drawer, and my name is Najiyah.
And a stab that sprays weakly,
I stabbed it at the chests of the enemies."

He said: While they were thus, Budayl ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i came with a group from his people. Khuza'ah were the trusted confidants of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the people of Tihamah. He said: "I left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy and 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, who have camped at the farthest waters of al-Hudaybiyyah, with their nursing camels and suckling young. They will fight you and bar you from the House."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We have not come to fight anyone, but we have come as pilgrims performing 'umrah. Quraysh has been exhausted by war and has been harmed by it. If they wish, we will make a truce with them for a period, and they will leave me to deal with the people. If I prevail, then good; and if they wish to enter into what the people have entered into, they may do so. Otherwise, they will have gathered their strength. By Allah, I will fight them for this matter of mine until my neck is severed, or until Allah makes His command prevail." [46] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 9/219; al-Musannaf: 5/333 with variation; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 20/11.]]

Budayl said: We will convey to them what you say.

He set off until he came to Quraysh and said: "We have come to you from this man, and we heard him say a statement. If you wish, we will present it to you." Their foolish ones said: "We have no need for you to tell us anything from him." Those of their men with opinion said: "Say what you heard him say." He said: "I heard him say such and such." He related to them what the Prophet (ﷺ) had said.

Then 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi stood and said: "O people, are you not the father's offspring?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Am I not the offspring?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Do you suspect me?" They said: "No." He said: "Do you not know that I summoned the people of 'Ukaz, and when they insisted upon me, I came to you with my family, my children, and those who obeyed me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "This man has presented you with a path of right guidance, so accept it and let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." So he went to him and began speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet said to him something similar to what he had said to Budayl. 'Urwah then said: "O Muhammad, do you think that if you destroy your own people, you have heard of anyone among the Arabs who has pillaged (and it is said: uprooted) his own people before you? And if the other outcome occurs, by Allah, I see faces and rabble from the people who I think will flee and abandon you."

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Suck the clitoris of al-Lat!" (al-Lat was the idol of Thaqif, which they used to worship.) "Shall we flee and abandon him?" 'Urwah said: "Who is this?" They said: "Abu Bakr." He said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, were it not for a favour you had done me, which I have not repaid, I would have answered you." He kept speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ), and whenever he spoke, he took hold of his beard. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah was standing over the head of the Messenger of Allah, carrying a sword and wearing a helmet. Whenever 'Urwah reached out his hand toward the beard of the Prophet (ﷺ), he struck his hand with the scabbard of the sword and said: "Remove your hand from his beard!" 'Urwah raised his head and said: "Who is this?" They said: "Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah." He said: "You treacherous one! Am I not still striving to rectify your treachery?" Al-Mughirah had accompanied some people in the pre-Islamic era, killed them, and taken their property, then he came and embraced Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "As for Islam, we have accepted it. As for the wealth, it is wealth obtained by treachery, and we have no need of it." [47] [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/629; Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/275.]]

'Urwah began to glance at the companions of the Messenger of Allah with his eyes. He said: "By Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) will not spit out phlegm except that it falls into the palm of one of them, so he rubs it over his face and skin. When he commands them, they rush to carry out his command. When he performs ablution, they nearly fight over his ablution water. When they speak, they lower their voices in his presence, and they do not look at him directly out of reverence for him."

'Urwah returned to his companions and said: "O people, I have been received by kings. I have been received by Caesar, Kisra, and the Negus. By Allah, I have never seen a king whom his companions honour as the companions of Muhammad honour Muhammad. By Allah, if he spits out phlegm, it falls into the palm of one of them, so he rubs it over his face and skin. When he commands them, they rush to carry out his command. When he performs ablution, they nearly fight over his ablution water. When they speak, they lower their voices, and they do not look at him directly out of reverence for him. He has presented you with a path of right guidance, so accept it."

A man from Kinanah said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came in sight of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, the Prophet said: "This is so-and-so, from a people who honour the sacrificial camels, so send them to him." They were sent to him, and a group came to meet him reciting the talbiyah. When he saw that, he said: "Glory be to Allah! It is not right that these people be barred from the House." Then they sent to him al-Juls ibn 'Alqamah ibn Rayyan, who was then the chief of the Ahabish. When the Messenger of Allah saw him, he (ﷺ) said: "This man is from a people who venerate (the sacred), so send the sacrificial camels in front of him, so that he may see them." [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/324.]]

When he saw the sacrificial animals flowing toward him from the side of the valley, with their garlands, having worn down their pegs from being held back for so long, he returned to Quraysh without reaching the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), out of awe at what he had seen. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh, I have seen what must not be barred: the sacrificial animals with their garlands, having worn down their pegs from being held back for so long from their place of sacrifice." They said to him: "Sit down, for you are only a bedouin with no knowledge." Al-Juls grew angry at that and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah, we did not ally with you on this basis, nor did we make a pact with you on this basis, that you should bar from the House of Allah one who comes to it glorifying it. By the One in whose hand is the soul of al-Juls, either you will let Muhammad and what he came for go free, or I will break away with the Ahabish, breaking away as one man." They said to him: "Hold back from us, O Juls, until we take for ourselves what we are content with."

A man among them called Mikraz ibn Hafs stood and said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came in sight of them, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is Mikraz ibn Hafs, and he is a wicked man." He began speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ), when Suhayl ibn 'Amr came. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw him, he said: "Your affair has been made easy for you. The people come to you with their kinship ties, asking you for peace. So send the sacrificial animals and display the talbiyah, perhaps that will soften their hearts." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 10/478.]] They recited the talbiyah from the corners of the camp until their voices resounded with the talbiyah. Then they came and asked for peace. Suhayl said: "Come, let us write a document between us and you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, and said to him: "Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." Suhayl said: "As for 'al-Rahman' (the Most Merciful), I do not know what it is. But write: 'In Your name, O Allah,' as you used to write." The Muslims said: "By Allah, we will not write it except as: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to 'Ali: "Write: 'In Your name, O Allah,' " then he said: "Write: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed upon." Suhayl said: "By Allah, if we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have barred you from the House, nor would we have fought you. But write your name and the name of your father."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I am indeed the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me." Then he said to 'Ali: "Erase 'Messenger of Allah'." 'Ali said: "By Allah, I will never erase you, ever." So the Messenger of Allah took it, and he did not know how to write, so he erased it himself. Then he said: "Write: This is what Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah has agreed upon with Suhayl ibn 'Amr, and they have agreed to put down war among the people for ten years, during which the people will be safe and will restrain some from others, and on the condition that whoever comes to Mecca from the companions of Muhammad as a pilgrim, or performing 'umrah, or seeking the bounty of Allah, will be safe in his life and property; and whoever comes to Medina from Quraysh, passing through to Egypt or to Syria seeking the bounty of Allah, will be safe in his life and property; and on the condition that whoever comes to the Messenger of Allah from Quraysh without the permission of his guardian, he will be returned to them; and whoever comes from those with the Messenger of Allah to Quraysh, they will not return him to him."

Thereupon this was grievous to the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever comes to them from among us, may Allah keep him far away; and whoever comes to us from among them, we will return him to them. Allah knows best what is in the heart of anyone who has embraced Islam, and will make a way out for him. Between us is a closed chest (of trust), and there is no secret theft and no shackles. Whoever wishes to enter into the covenant and pact of Muhammad, may enter it; and whoever wishes to enter into the covenant and pact of Quraysh, may enter it." [48] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/325; al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/192.]]

So Khuza'ah sprang up and said: "We are within the covenant and pact of Muhammad." And Banu Bakr sprang up and said: "We are within the covenant and pact of Quraysh." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And on condition that they leave us free between us and the House, so that we may circumambulate it." Suhayl said: "The Arabs will not say that we were subdued by force. But this will be yours in the coming year." So he wrote: "And on condition that you turn back from us this year, and do not enter Makkah against us; and when next year comes, we will withdraw from it for you, and you may enter it with your companions and remain there three days, and enter it with no weapons except swords in their sheaths, and the arms of a rider. And on condition that this sacrificial animal is to be slaughtered wherever we are prevented from reaching it, and you shall not bring it forward against us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "We will drive it, and you will turn back its faces." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 10/480; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/125.]]

He said: While the Messenger of Allah was writing the document, he and Suhayl ibn 'Amr, there suddenly came Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn 'Amr, dragging his shackles, having escaped and come out from the lower part of Makkah until he threw himself among the Muslims. When Suhayl saw Abu Jandal, he stood up to him, struck his face, seized his chain, and said: "O Muhammad, the agreement between me and you has been concluded before this man came to you, and this is the first man I will hold you to it over. Will you return him to us?" Then he began to drag him to return him to Quraysh. Abu Jandal cried out at the top of his voice: "O company of Muslims, am I to be returned to the polytheists, when I have come as a Muslim? Do you not see what I have suffered?" He had been severely tortured for the sake of Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Jandal, be patient and seek your reward, for Allah will surely make a relief and a way out for you and for those with you among the oppressed. We have made a covenant between us and these people, and a treaty, and we have given them that on condition, and they have given us a pledge. We will not betray them." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/282.]]

'Umar ibn al-Khattab then leapt to Abu Jandal, walking beside him and saying: "Be patient, O Abu Jandal, for they are only polytheists, and the blood of one of them is the blood of a dog," and he brought the edge of the sword close to him. He said: 'Umar said: "I hoped he would take the sword and strike his father with it, but the man refused to harm his father."

They said: The companions of the Messenger of Allah had set out, not doubting the conquest, because of a dream the Messenger of Allah had seen. When they saw this, a great distress came upon the people, until they nearly perished, and the matter of Abu Jandal added evil to what they already suffered. 'Umar said: "By Allah, I have had no doubt since I embraced Islam until that day. So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Are you not the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?'"

He said: "I am the Messenger of Allah, and I do not disobey Him, and He is my helper." [49] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 20/14; Irwa' al-Ghalil: 1/58.]]

'Umar said: "Did you not tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Did I inform you that we would come to it this year?" I said: "No." He said: "Then you will come to it and circumambulate it." 'Umar said: "Then I came to Abu Bakr and said: 'Is this not truly the Prophet of Allah?'"

He said: "Yes." I said: "Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?" I said: "Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?" He said: "O man, he is the Messenger of Allah, and he does not disobey his Lord. Hold fast to his stirrup until you die, for by Allah he is upon the truth." I said: "Did he not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Did I inform you that you would come to it this year?" I said: "No." He said: "Then you will come to it and circumambulate it." 'Umar said: "I continued to fast, give charity, pray, and free slaves, because of what I did that day, fearing for the words I had spoken."

They said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had finished the document, he called upon men as witnesses to the treaty, from among the Muslims and from among the polytheists: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, 'Abd Allah ibn Suhayl ibn 'Amr, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Mahmud ibn Maslamah, brother of Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, Mikraz ibn Hafs ibn al-Ahnaf, who was a polytheist, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was the scribe of the document.

When the Messenger of Allah had finished his affair, he set out with the sacrificial animals, and the people set out. When the sacrificial animals reached a point short of the mountains that overlook the valley of al-Thaniyyah, the polytheists confronted them and turned their faces back. The Prophet (ﷺ) stopped where they had been held, which was al-Hudaybiyah, and said to his companions: "Stand up, slaughter, then shave your heads." He said: "By Allah, not one of them stood up."

He said this three times, and when none of them stood up, he went in and entered upon Umm Salamah, and told her what he had suffered from the people.

Umm Salamah said: "O Prophet of Allah, go out, and do not speak a word to any of them until you slaughter your camel and call your barber to shave you." So he went out and did not speak a word to any of them until he slaughtered his camel, and called his barber, who shaved him. The one who shaved him that day was Khirash ibn Umayyah ibn al-Fadl al-Khuza'i. On the day of al-Hudaybiyah, some men shaved and others cut short. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on those who shaved." They said: "And those who cut short, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "May Allah have mercy on those who shaved." They said: "And those who cut short, O Messenger of Allah?" 

They said: "Why did you single out those who shaved for mercy, rather than those who cut short?" He said: "Because they did not doubt." Ibn 'Umar said: "That was because the people had grown calm, and they said: 'Perhaps we will circumambulate the House.'"

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent, in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, among his sacrificial animals, a camel that belonged to Abu Jahl, with a silver ring in its nose, to enrage the polytheists by this. Then there came to him (ﷺ) believing women, and Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿O you who have believed, when there come to you the believing women emigrating...﴾ [[Surat al-Mumtahanah: 10.]] ... the verse. He said: So 'Umar divorced two wives he had who were in polytheism. He said: Then He forbade them to return them, and commanded that the dowries be returned at that time. A man said to al-Zuhri: "Was it because of the women?" He said: "Yes." So one of them was married by Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and the other by Safwan ibn Umayyah.

Then the Prophet (ﷺ) returned to Madinah. Abu Basir 'Utbah ibn Usayd ibn Harithah came to him, and he was a Muslim, and he had been among those who remained in Makkah. Azhar ibn 'Abd 'Awf and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi wrote concerning him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and sent a man from Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, with a mawla (freedman) of theirs, and they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with their letter, and said: "The covenant you made for us..."
