When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw him approaching, he said: "This man has seen something frightening."

When he reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Woe to you, what is wrong with you?" He said: "Your companion has killed my companion." By Allah, he had hardly finished when Abu Basir arrived, girded with his sword, and stood before the Messenger of Allah, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have fulfilled your covenant, you handed me over to them, and - it was said: and returned me to them - then Allah rescued me from them." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Woe to his mother, he is a kindler of war. If only he had men with him."

When he heard that, he knew that he would return him to them. So Abu Basir went out until he came to the coast of the sea, and stopped at al-Ghayd, near Dhu'l-Marwah, on the sea shore, on the route of Quraysh which they used to take to Syria. The Muslims who had been held back in Makkah heard the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) concerning Abu Basir: "Woe to his mother, he is a kindler of war, if only he had men with him." So a band of them went out to him, and Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn 'Amr escaped and joined Abu Basir, until about seventy men gathered to him. By Allah, they did not hear of a caravan going out from Quraysh to Syria without intercepting it, killing them and taking their wealth, until they constrained Quraysh. So Quraysh sent to the Prophet (ﷺ) (peace be upon him), begging him by Allah and by kinship, to send for them, and whoever came to him would be safe. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them refuge, and they came to him in Madinah. [51] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/285.]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, whom you might trample and thereby incur from them a cost without knowledge...﴾ Ibn Zayd said: "Sin." Ibn Ishaq said: "The payment of blood money." It was also said: "Expiation, because Allah the Exalted only obligated the killer of a believer in the land of war, if he had not emigrated from it and his killer did not know his faith, the expiation rather than the blood money." So the Majestic One said: ﴿And if he was from a people hostile to you and he was a believer, then [the freeing of] a believing slave﴾ [[Surat al-Nisa': 92.]] 

And He did not obligate blood money for the killer by mistake. It was also said: it is that the polytheists would blame you, saying: "They have killed people of their own religion." (The "ma'arrah" is hardship, and its origin is from al-'arr, which is war, because the permission to enter it was granted, but He prevented you from that.) ﴿That Allah admits into His mercy whom He wills﴾ of the people of Makkah, from among those who entered Islam before you entered it. This is the arrangement and ruling of the verse, so the answer to "lawla" (if not) is omitted, being understood from the context. Some scholars said: His saying ﴿We would have punished﴾ is the answer to two statements: the first is ﴿if not for believing men﴾, and the second is ﴿if they had been distinguished﴾, meaning separated.

Then He said: ﴿That Allah admits into His mercy whom He wills﴾, meaning the believing men and believing women, ﴿into His mercy﴾, that is, His Paradise. Qatadah said: In this verse, Allah repels the disbelievers by means of believers, just as He repels from the polytheists of Makkah by means of the weak among the believers.

We were informed by Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Manjuwayh al-Dinawari, we were told by Abu 'Ali ibn Habash al-Muqri, we were told by Abu al-Tayyib Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bajli al-Darimi in Antioch, I was told by Ahmad ibn Ya'qub al-Dinawari, we were told by Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Ansari, I was told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ja'fari, who said: I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrating, from his father, from his grandfather 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, that he asked [the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)] about the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿If they had been distinguished, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with painful punishment.﴾ He said: "They are the polytheists, from the forefathers of the Prophet (ﷺ), and those who came after him in his era. In their loins were believers, so if the believers had been separated from the loins of the disbelievers, Allah would have punished them with a painful punishment." [52]

Because it relates to His saying: ﴿We would have punished, when those who disbelieved put into their hearts zealotry - the zealotry of ignorance﴾, when they barred the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions from the House, and did not acknowledge ﴿In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾, nor the messengership of the Messenger of Allah. (The "hamiyyah", zealotry, is of the form fa'iliyyah, from the saying of the speaker: "Fulan protected his nose (hamiya anfahu), he protects with zealotry and protection." Al-Mutalammis said:

"Indeed I am among them, and my honour is their honour,
Just as the head protects its nose from being broken."

That is, it prevents. ﴿So Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and He made them adhere to the word of righteousness﴾, meaning sincerity. Its parallels are His saying: ﴿But it is piety from you that reaches Him﴾ [[Surat al-Hajj: 37.]] and His saying: ﴿Allah only accepts from the righteous﴾ [[Surat al-Ma'idah: 27.]].

We were informed by Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Shadhan al-Razi, in my reading to him, we were told by Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi al-Rabi' al-Qattan, we were told by 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hanbal, and Haytham - or Wahdam - ibn Hammam al-Amuli, and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd, they said: We were told by al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah, we were told by Sufyan ibn Habib, we were told by Shu'bah, from Yazid ibn Abi Najiyah, from al-Tufayl ibn Abi, from his father, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and He made them adhere to the word of righteousness﴾: "There is no god but Allah." [53] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/138; Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/63.]]

This is also the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, 'Amr ibn Maymun, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Salamah ibn Kuhayl, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, 'Ikrimah, Talhah ibn Musarrif, al-Rabi', al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: it is "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

We were informed by 'Abd al-Khaliq ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq, we were informed by Abu Bakr ibn Habib, we were told by Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Muzani, we were told by Abu Nu'aym and Abu Hudhayfah, who both said: we were told by Sufyan, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from 'Ayyash ibn Rabi'i, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning ﴿and He made them adhere to the word of righteousness﴾, that he said: "There is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest."

This is also the saying of Ibn 'Umar. 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: it is "There is no god but Allah alone, without partner, to Him belongs the dominion, to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things competent."

We were informed by Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun, we were informed by Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid, we were told by Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi in Nishapur, we were told by Salamah ibn Sulaym al-Sulami, we were told by 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, concerning ﴿and He made them adhere to the word of righteousness﴾, that he said: "In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful."

﴿And they were more worthy of it and deserving of it, and Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger Muhammad (peace be upon him) the vision that he saw concerning his departure to al-Hudaybiyah, that he and his companions would enter the Sacred Mosque. ﴿Certainly will Allah fulfil for His Messenger the vision in truth. You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in safety, with your heads shaved and hair shortened, not fearing.﴾ His saying "surely will enter" means: and he said "surely will enter", because the expression "the vision" is a statement. Ibn Kaysan said: His saying "surely will enter" is from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to his companions, relating his vision; so Allah the Exalted informed about His Messenger that he said that, and for this reason he made the exception out of courtesy with the courtesy of Allah the Exalted, when He said to him: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," except [with the qualification], "If Allah wills."﴾ [[Surat al-Kahf: 23.]] Abu 'Ubaydah said: "in" (in) means "when" (idh), its meaning being "when Allah wills," as in His saying: ﴿if you are believers﴾, and ﴿if they desire chastity﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 33.]].

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: It is permissible that the exception relates to the entering, because between the "vision" and its fulfilment there was a year, and some of them died during the year. So the meaning of the verse is: "You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, all of you, if Allah wills, in safety."

It is also permissible that the exception applies to the fear and the safety, not to the entering, because there was no doubt about the entering. For the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying when entering the graveyard: "And we, if Allah wills, will surely join you." [54] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/493, hadith 1547.]] So the exception applies to joining, not to death.

﴿So He knew what you did not know﴾, that the good lay in the treaty, which is His saying: ﴿And if not for believing men...﴾ [the verse]. ﴿And He gave, besides that, a near victory﴾, that is, besides their entering the Sacred Mosque and the fulfilment of the Messenger of Allah's vision. According to most exegetes, it is the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah. Al-Zuhri said: No conquest in Islam was greater than the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, because fighting had been where people met; but when the truce came, war was set aside, people were secure with one another, and they met and conversed and debated. No one who spoke with intelligence about Islam was not drawn into it in those two years, and more than had been in Islam before that.

Ibn Zayd said: It is the conquest of Khaybar, which Allah, exalted is He, granted them when they returned from al-Hudaybiyah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided it among all the people of al-Hudaybiyah except one man from the Ansar, namely Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah, who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyah but was absent from Khaybar.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (*al-Jawahir al-Hisan*) on surah 48, verses 22–27 (part 1 of 3):

﴿And if those who disbelieve fought you, they would surely turn their backs; then they would find neither a protector nor a helper.﴾ He means Asad, Ghatafan, and the people of Khaybar. Qatadah said: He means the disbelievers of Quraysh. ﴿The way of Allah, which has already passed before, and you will not find any change in the way of Allah.﴾ That is, like the way of Allah which has passed before, in granting victory to His friends and subduing His enemies. ﴿And He is the One who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the heart of Mecca,﴾ that is, al-Hudaybiyyah, ﴿after He had given you victory over them. And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do.﴾ (*al-Ya'*) Abu 'Amr and others read it with *ya'* (they), and others read it with *ta'* (you). They differed concerning who they were. Anas said: Eighty men from the people of Mecca descended upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions from the mountain of al-Tan'im at the time of the dawn prayer during the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, intending to kill them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took them alive and set them free. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And He is the One who withheld their hands from you…﴾ to the end of the verse.

'Ikrimah related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Quraysh had sent forty or fifty men from among them, and ordered them to circle around the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, to strike some of his companions, but they were seized. They were brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he pardoned them and released them. They had been pelting the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with stones and arrows. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And He is the One who withheld their hands from you…﴾ to the end of the verse.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughaffal said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) at al-Hudaybiyyah, beneath the root of a tree, and a branch of that tree was on his back. I lifted it from his back. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib was before him writing the treaty of peace, and Suhayl ibn 'Amr was there. Thirty young men came out to us armed, and they rushed at us. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) invoked Allah, and Allah blinded their sight. We stood up to them, seized them, and the Messenger of Allah released them. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse. [39] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/281.]]

Mujahid said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) came out intending to perform 'umrah, and his companions seized some people from the sanctuary who were unaware. The Prophet (ﷺ) released them. That is the "victory" in ﴿the heart of Mecca﴾.

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that a man among the companions of the Messenger of Allah, called Zunaym, looked out from the pass of al-Hudaybiyyah. The polytheists shot him with an arrow and killed him. The Messenger of Allah sent cavalry, and they brought twelve disbelieving horsemen. The Prophet of Allah said to them: "Do you have a covenant with me? Do you have a pact with me?" [40] They said: No. So he released them, and Allah revealed this verse.

Ibn Ayzi and al-Kalbi said: They were the people of al-Hudaybiyyah. When the Prophet (ﷺ) set out with the sacrificial animals and reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: "O Prophet of Allah, will you enter upon a people who are at war with you without weapons or horses?" He sent to Medina, and he left no horse or weapon there without taking it. When he approached Mecca, they prevented him from entering. He went on until he came to Mina, and he stayed at Mina. Then a spy came to him saying that 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl had come out against you with five hundred men. He said to Khalid ibn al-Walid: "O Khalid, this is your cousin who has come to you with horses." Khalid said: "I am the sword of Allah and the sword of His Messenger, O Messenger of Allah, send me wherever you wish." On that day he was named "the Sword of Allah." He sent him with cavalry, and he met 'Ikrimah in the ravine and defeated him until he drove him into the walls of Mecca. Then they returned a second time, and he defeated him until he drove him into the walls of Mecca. Then he returned a third time, and he defeated him until he drove him into the walls of Mecca. So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And He is the One who withheld their hands from you…﴾ to His saying ﴿a painful punishment﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) withheld from the remnants of the Muslims who had remained there after He had granted him victory over them, out of aversion that the horses might trample them without knowledge. [41] This is His saying: ﴿They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and the sacrificial animals detained from reaching their place of sacrifice.﴾ That is, they barred the sacrificial animals, held back. [42] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/123.]]

﴿from reaching their place of sacrifice﴾, that is, their place of slaughter. They were seventy camels.

Al-Zuhri related, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who both said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) left Medina in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, intending to visit the House, not intending fighting. He took with him seventy camels, and the people were seven hundred men, so each camel was for ten persons. When he reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, people joined him, and he set out with some hundreds of his companions. When they were at Dhu al-Hulayfah, he garlanded the sacrificial animals, marked them, and entered into the state of ihram for 'umrah. He sent ahead a spy from Khuza'ah to inform him about Quraysh.

The Prophet (ﷺ) continued until, when he was at the pool of al-Ashtat, near 'Usfan, the Khuza'i spy came to him and said: "I left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy and 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, who have gathered the Ahabish for you. They will fight you and bar you from the House." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Advise me. Do you think we should attack the offspring of those who assisted them and take them captive? If they remain seated, they will sit as men who have been wronged, and if they escape, it will be a neck which Allah has cut off. Or do you think we should head for the House, and whoever bars us from it, we will fight him?"

Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have not come to fight anyone, but whoever stands between us and the House, we will fight him." The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Then set out."

Abu Hurayrah used to say: I never saw anyone more consultative with his companions than the Prophet (ﷺ). They set out until, when they were at 'Usfan, Bishr ibn Sufyan al-Ka'bi met him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, these are Quraysh. They have heard of your journey, so they have come out with their nursing camels and their suckling young, wearing leopard skins. They have camped at Dhu Tuwa, swearing by Allah that you will never enter upon them. And this is Khalid ibn al-Walid with their horses, who have advanced them to Kura' al-Ghamim." I have mentioned the saying of one who said: On that day Khalid ibn al-Walid was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as a Muslim. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Woe to Quraysh! War has consumed them. What harm would it do them if they left me between myself and the rest of the Arabs? If they overcome me, that is what they wanted, and if Allah makes me victorious over them, they will enter Islam in multitudes, and if they do not do that, they will fight while still possessing strength. What does Quraysh think? By Allah, I will not cease to strive against them for the sake of what Allah has sent me with, until Allah makes it prevail, or my neck is severed." [43] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/323; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 20/16.]]

Then he said: "Who will lead us by a route other than the one they are on?" A man from Aslam said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." So he led them on a rough, difficult path between ravines. When they came out of it, the Muslims had found that burdensome, and it led to a level land at the end of the valley. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the people: "Say: We seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him." They did so, and he said: "By Allah, this is the 'hittah' (remission) that was presented to the Children of Israel, but they did not say it." [44] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/273; al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 4/189.]]

Then the Messenger of Allah said to the people: "Take the route to the right," along a path that leads out at the pass of al-Murar, descending upon al-Hudaybiyyah from the lower part of Mecca.

The army took that route. When the horsemen of Quraysh saw the departure of Quraysh (from its own route) and that the Messenger of Allah had diverged from their path, they spurred back to Quraysh to warn them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued until, when he took the pass of al-Murar, his she-camel knelt down with him. The people said: "Hal, hal!" He said: "What is 'hal'?" They said: "She has been made to stop, by force." He said: "She has not been made to stop, and that is not her habit, but the one who stopped the elephant has stopped her." [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/323; Sahih al-Bukhari: 3/178 with variation; Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/629.]] [45]

Then he said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, Quraysh will not ask me today for any arrangement by which they glorify the sacred things of Allah, and in which there is the maintenance of kinship, except that I will give it to them." Then he said to the people: "Dismount." They dismounted at the farthest part of al-Hudaybiyyah, at a well of little water, from which people could only take water in small amounts. The people soon exhausted it. The people complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of thirst. He drew an arrow from his quiver and gave it to a man of his companions called Najiyah ibn 'Umayr ibn Ya'mur ibn Darim, who was the driver of the sacrificial camels of the Messenger of Allah. He descended into that well and thrust it into its bottom, and the water gushed forth with abundance, until they departed from it. It is said that a girl from the Ansar came with her bucket, while Najiyah was in the well drawing water for the people, and she said:

"O you who draw water, my bucket is yours,
for I see the people praising you,
extolling your goodness and glorifying you;
I hope for good from you as they hope from you."

He said:

"The Yemeni girl knows
that I am the drawer, and my name is Najiyah.
And a stab that sprays weakly,
I stabbed it at the chests of the enemies."

He said: While they were thus, Budayl ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i came with a group from his people. Khuza'ah were the trusted confidants of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the people of Tihamah. He said: "I left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy and 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, who have camped at the farthest waters of al-Hudaybiyyah, with their nursing camels and suckling young. They will fight you and bar you from the House."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We have not come to fight anyone, but we have come as pilgrims performing 'umrah. Quraysh has been exhausted by war and has been harmed by it. If they wish, we will make a truce with them for a period, and they will leave me to deal with the people. If I prevail, then good; and if they wish to enter into what the people have entered into, they may do so. Otherwise, they will have gathered their strength. By Allah, I will fight them for this matter of mine until my neck is severed, or until Allah makes His command prevail." [46] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 9/219; al-Musannaf: 5/333 with variation; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 20/11.]]

Budayl said: We will convey to them what you say.

He set off until he came to Quraysh and said: "We have come to you from this man, and we heard him say a statement. If you wish, we will present it to you." Their foolish ones said: "We have no need for you to tell us anything from him." Those of their men with opinion said: "Say what you heard him say." He said: "I heard him say such and such." He related to them what the Prophet (ﷺ) had said.

Then 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi stood and said: "O people, are you not the father's offspring?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Am I not the offspring?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Do you suspect me?" They said: "No." He said: "Do you not know that I summoned the people of 'Ukaz, and when they insisted upon me, I came to you with my family, my children, and those who obeyed me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "This man has presented you with a path of right guidance, so accept it and let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." So he went to him and began speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet said to him something similar to what he had said to Budayl. 'Urwah then said: "O Muhammad, do you think that if you destroy your own people, you have heard of anyone among the Arabs who has pillaged (and it is said: uprooted) his own people before you? And if the other outcome occurs, by Allah, I see faces and rabble from the people who I think will flee and abandon you."

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Suck the clitoris of al-Lat!" (al-Lat was the idol of Thaqif, which they used to worship.) "Shall we flee and abandon him?" 'Urwah said: "Who is this?" They said: "Abu Bakr." He said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, were it not for a favour you had done me, which I have not repaid, I would have answered you." He kept speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ), and whenever he spoke, he took hold of his beard. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah was standing over the head of the Messenger of Allah, carrying a sword and wearing a helmet. Whenever 'Urwah reached out his hand toward the beard of the Prophet (ﷺ), he struck his hand with the scabbard of the sword and said: "Remove your hand from his beard!" 'Urwah raised his head and said: "Who is this?" They said: "Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah." He said: "You treacherous one! Am I not still striving to rectify your treachery?" Al-Mughirah had accompanied some people in the pre-Islamic era, killed them, and taken their property, then he came and embraced Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "As for Islam, we have accepted it. As for the wealth, it is wealth obtained by treachery, and we have no need of it." [47] [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/629; Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/275.]]

'Urwah began to glance at the companions of the Messenger of Allah with his eyes. He said: "By Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) will not spit out phlegm except that it falls into the palm of one of them, so he rubs it over his face and skin. When he commands them, they rush to carry out his command. When he performs ablution, they nearly fight over his ablution water. When they speak, they lower their voices in his presence, and they do not look at him directly out of reverence for him."

'Urwah returned to his companions and said: "O people, I have been received by kings. I have been received by Caesar, Kisra, and the Negus. By Allah, I have never seen a king whom his companions honour as the companions of Muhammad honour Muhammad. By Allah, if he spits out phlegm, it falls into the palm of one of them, so he rubs it over his face and skin. When he commands them, they rush to carry out his command. When he performs ablution, they nearly fight over his ablution water. When they speak, they lower their voices, and they do not look at him directly out of reverence for him. He has presented you with a path of right guidance, so accept it."

A man from Kinanah said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came in sight of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, the Prophet said: "This is so-and-so, from a people who honour the sacrificial camels, so send them to him." They were sent to him, and a group came to meet him reciting the talbiyah. When he saw that, he said: "Glory be to Allah! It is not right that these people be barred from the House." Then they sent to him al-Juls ibn 'Alqamah ibn Rayyan, who was then the chief of the Ahabish. When the Messenger of Allah saw him, he (ﷺ) said: "This man is from a people who venerate (the sacred), so send the sacrificial camels in front of him, so that he may see them." [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/324.]]

When he saw the sacrificial animals flowing toward him from the side of the valley, with their garlands, having worn down their pegs from being held back for so long, he returned to Quraysh without reaching the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), out of awe at what he had seen. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh, I have seen what must not be barred: the sacrificial animals with their garlands, having worn down their pegs from being held back for so long from their place of sacrifice." They said to him: "Sit down, for you are only a bedouin with no knowledge." Al-Juls grew angry at that and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah, we did not ally with you on this basis, nor did we make a pact with you on this basis, that you should bar from the House of Allah one who comes to it glorifying it. By the One in whose hand is the soul of al-Juls, either you will let Muhammad and what he came for go free, or I will break away with the Ahabish, breaking away as one man." They said to him: "Hold back from us, O Juls, until we take for ourselves what we are content with."

A man among them called Mikraz ibn Hafs stood and said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came in sight of them, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is Mikraz ibn Hafs, and he is a wicked man." He began speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ), when Suhayl ibn 'Amr came. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw him, he said: "Your affair has been made easy for you. The people come to you with their kinship ties, asking you for peace. So send the sacrificial animals and display the talbiyah, perhaps that will soften their hearts." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 10/478.]] They recited the talbiyah from the corners of the camp until their voices resounded with the talbiyah. Then they came and asked for peace. Suhayl said: "Come, let us write a document between us and you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, and said to him: "Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." Suhayl said: "As for 'al-Rahman' (the Most Merciful), I do not know what it is. But write: 'In Your name, O Allah,' as you used to write." The Muslims said: "By Allah, we will not write it except as: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to 'Ali: "Write: 'In Your name, O Allah,' " then he said: "Write: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed upon." Suhayl said: "By Allah, if we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have barred you from the House, nor would we have fought you. But write your name and the name of your father."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I am indeed the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me." Then he said to 'Ali: "Erase 'Messenger of Allah'." 'Ali said: "By Allah, I will never erase you, ever." So the Messenger of Allah took it, and he did not know how to write, so he erased it himself. Then he said: "Write: This is what Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah has agreed upon with Suhayl ibn 'Amr, and they have agreed to put down war among the people for ten years, during which the people will be safe and will restrain some from others, and on the condition that whoever comes to Mecca from the companions of Muhammad as a pilgrim, or performing 'umrah, or seeking the bounty of Allah, will be safe in his life and property; and whoever comes to Medina from Quraysh, passing through to Egypt or to Syria seeking the bounty of Allah, will be safe in his life and property; and on the condition that whoever comes to the Messenger of Allah from Quraysh without the permission of his guardian, he will be returned to them; and whoever comes from those with the Messenger of Allah to Quraysh, they will not return him to him."

Thereupon this was grievous to the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever comes to them from among us, may Allah keep him far away; and whoever comes to us from among them, we will return him to them. Allah knows best what is in the heart of anyone who has embraced Islam, and will make a way out for him. Between us is a closed chest (of trust), and there is no secret theft and no shackles. Whoever wishes to enter into the covenant and pact of Muhammad, may enter it; and whoever wishes to enter into the covenant and pact of Quraysh, may enter it." [48] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/325; al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/192.]]

So Khuza'ah sprang up and said: "We are within the covenant and pact of Muhammad." And Banu Bakr sprang up and said: "We are within the covenant and pact of Quraysh." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And on condition that they leave us free between us and the House, so that we may circumambulate it." Suhayl said: "The Arabs will not say that we were subdued by force. But this will be yours in the coming year." So he wrote: "And on condition that you turn back from us this year, and do not enter Makkah against us; and when next year comes, we will withdraw from it for you, and you may enter it with your companions and remain there three days, and enter it with no weapons except swords in their sheaths, and the arms of a rider. And on condition that this sacrificial animal is to be slaughtered wherever we are prevented from reaching it, and you shall not bring it forward against us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "We will drive it, and you will turn back its faces." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 10/480; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/125.]]

He said: While the Messenger of Allah was writing the document, he and Suhayl ibn 'Amr, there suddenly came Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn 'Amr, dragging his shackles, having escaped and come out from the lower part of Makkah until he threw himself among the Muslims. When Suhayl saw Abu Jandal, he stood up to him, struck his face, seized his chain, and said: "O Muhammad, the agreement between me and you has been concluded before this man came to you, and this is the first man I will hold you to it over. Will you return him to us?" Then he began to drag him to return him to Quraysh. Abu Jandal cried out at the top of his voice: "O company of Muslims, am I to be returned to the polytheists, when I have come as a Muslim? Do you not see what I have suffered?" He had been severely tortured for the sake of Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Jandal, be patient and seek your reward, for Allah will surely make a relief and a way out for you and for those with you among the oppressed. We have made a covenant between us and these people, and a treaty, and we have given them that on condition, and they have given us a pledge. We will not betray them." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/282.]]

'Umar ibn al-Khattab then leapt to Abu Jandal, walking beside him and saying: "Be patient, O Abu Jandal, for they are only polytheists, and the blood of one of them is the blood of a dog," and he brought the edge of the sword close to him. He said: 'Umar said: "I hoped he would take the sword and strike his father with it, but the man refused to harm his father."

They said: The companions of the Messenger of Allah had set out, not doubting the conquest, because of a dream the Messenger of Allah had seen. When they saw this, a great distress came upon the people, until they nearly perished, and the matter of Abu Jandal added evil to what they already suffered. 'Umar said: "By Allah, I have had no doubt since I embraced Islam until that day. So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Are you not the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?'"

He said: "I am the Messenger of Allah, and I do not disobey Him, and He is my helper." [49] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 20/14; Irwa' al-Ghalil: 1/58.]]

'Umar said: "Did you not tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Did I inform you that we would come to it this year?" I said: "No." He said: "Then you will come to it and circumambulate it." 'Umar said: "Then I came to Abu Bakr and said: 'Is this not truly the Prophet of Allah?'"

He said: "Yes." I said: "Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?" I said: "Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?" He said: "O man, he is the Messenger of Allah, and he does not disobey his Lord. Hold fast to his stirrup until you die, for by Allah he is upon the truth." I said: "Did he not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Did I inform you that you would come to it this year?" I said: "No." He said: "Then you will come to it and circumambulate it." 'Umar said: "I continued to fast, give charity, pray, and free slaves, because of what I did that day, fearing for the words I had spoken."

They said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had finished the document, he called upon men as witnesses to the treaty, from among the Muslims and from among the polytheists: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, 'Abd Allah ibn Suhayl ibn 'Amr, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Mahmud ibn Maslamah, brother of Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, Mikraz ibn Hafs ibn al-Ahnaf, who was a polytheist, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was the scribe of the document.

When the Messenger of Allah had finished his affair, he set out with the sacrificial animals, and the people set out. When the sacrificial animals reached a point short of the mountains that overlook the valley of al-Thaniyyah, the polytheists confronted them and turned their faces back. The Prophet (ﷺ) stopped where they had been held, which was al-Hudaybiyah, and said to his companions: "Stand up, slaughter, then shave your heads." He said: "By Allah, not one of them stood up."

He said this three times, and when none of them stood up, he went in and entered upon Umm Salamah, and told her what he had suffered from the people.

Umm Salamah said: "O Prophet of Allah, go out, and do not speak a word to any of them until you slaughter your camel and call your barber to shave you." So he went out and did not speak a word to any of them until he slaughtered his camel, and called his barber, who shaved him. The one who shaved him that day was Khirash ibn Umayyah ibn al-Fadl al-Khuza'i. On the day of al-Hudaybiyah, some men shaved and others cut short. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on those who shaved." They said: "And those who cut short, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "May Allah have mercy on those who shaved." They said: "And those who cut short, O Messenger of Allah?" 

They said: "Why did you single out those who shaved for mercy, rather than those who cut short?" He said: "Because they did not doubt." Ibn 'Umar said: "That was because the people had grown calm, and they said: 'Perhaps we will circumambulate the House.'"

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent, in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, among his sacrificial animals, a camel that belonged to Abu Jahl, with a silver ring in its nose, to enrage the polytheists by this. Then there came to him (ﷺ) believing women, and Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿O you who have believed, when there come to you the believing women emigrating...﴾ [[Surat al-Mumtahanah: 10.]] ... the verse. He said: So 'Umar divorced two wives he had who were in polytheism. He said: Then He forbade them to return them, and commanded that the dowries be returned at that time. A man said to al-Zuhri: "Was it because of the women?" He said: "Yes." So one of them was married by Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and the other by Safwan ibn Umayyah.

Then the Prophet (ﷺ) returned to Madinah. Abu Basir 'Utbah ibn Usayd ibn Harithah came to him, and he was a Muslim, and he had been among those who remained in Makkah. Azhar ibn 'Abd 'Awf and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi wrote concerning him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and sent a man from Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, with a mawla (freedman) of theirs, and they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with their letter, and said: "The covenant you made for us..." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Basir, we have given these people what you know, and it is not right for us in our religion to betray. Allah the Exalted will surely make a relief and a way out for you and for those with you among the oppressed." [50] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/283-284.]]

Then he handed him over to the two men, and they set out with him until, when they reached Dhu'l-Hulayfah, they stopped to eat dates they had. Abu Basir said to one of the two men: "By Allah, I see that your sword is fine." The other drew it, and said: "Indeed, by Allah, it is fine." He said: "Let me look at it." So he took it and struck the brother of Banu 'Amir with it until he killed him. The mawla fled, and went quickly until he came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), while he was sitting in the mosque. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw him approaching, he said: "This man has seen something frightening."

When he reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Woe to you, what is wrong with you?" He said: "Your companion has killed my companion." By Allah, he had hardly finished when Abu Basir arrived, girded with his sword, and stood before the Messenger of Allah, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have fulfilled your covenant, you handed me over to them, and - it was said: and returned me to them - then Allah rescued me from them." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Woe to his mother, he is a kindler of war. If only he had men with him."

When he heard that, he knew that he would return him to them. So Abu Basir went out until he came to the coast of the sea, and stopped at al-Ghayd, near Dhu'l-Marwah, on the sea shore, on the route of Quraysh which they used to take to Syria. The Muslims who had been held back in Makkah heard the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) concerning Abu Basir: "Woe to his mother, he is a kindler of war, if only he had men with him." So a band of them went out to him, and Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn 'Amr escaped and joined Abu Basir, until about seventy men gathered to him. By Allah, they did not hear of a caravan going out from Quraysh to Syria without intercepting it, killing them and taking their wealth, until they constrained Quraysh. So Quraysh sent to the Prophet (ﷺ) (peace be upon him), begging him by Allah and by kinship, to send for them, and whoever came to him would be safe. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them refuge, and they came to him in Madinah. [51] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/285.]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, whom you might trample and thereby incur from them a cost without knowledge...﴾ Ibn Zayd said: "Sin." Ibn Ishaq said: "The payment of blood money." It was also said: "Expiation, because Allah the Exalted only obligated the killer of a believer in the land of war, if he had not emigrated from it and his killer did not know his faith, the expiation rather than the blood money." So the Majestic One said: ﴿And if he was from a people hostile to you and he was a believer, then [the freeing of] a believing slave﴾ [[Surat al-Nisa': 92.]] 

And He did not obligate blood money for the killer by mistake. It was also said: it is that the polytheists would blame you, saying: "They have killed people of their own religion." (The "ma'arrah" is hardship, and its origin is from al-'arr, which is war, because the permission to enter it was granted, but He prevented you from that.) ﴿That Allah admits into His mercy whom He wills﴾ of the people of Makkah, from among those who entered Islam before you entered it. This is the arrangement and ruling of the verse, so the answer to "lawla" (if not) is omitted, being understood from the context. Some scholars said: His saying ﴿We would have punished﴾ is the answer to two statements: the first is ﴿if not for believing men﴾, and the second is ﴿if they had been distinguished﴾, meaning separated.

Then He said: ﴿That Allah admits into His mercy whom He wills﴾, meaning the believing men and believing women, ﴿into His mercy﴾, that is, His Paradise. Qatadah said: In this verse, Allah repels the disbelievers by means of believers, just as He repels from the polytheists of Makkah by means of the weak among the believers.

We were informed by Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Manjuwayh al-Dinawari, we were told by Abu 'Ali ibn Habash al-Muqri, we were told by Abu al-Tayyib Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bajli al-Darimi in Antioch, I was told by Ahmad ibn Ya'qub al-Dinawari, we were told by Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Ansari, I was told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ja'fari, who said: I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrating, from his father, from his grandfather 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, that he asked [the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)] about the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿If they had been distinguished, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with painful punishment.﴾ He said: "They are the polytheists, from the forefathers of the Prophet (ﷺ), and those who came after him in his era. In their loins were believers, so if the believers had been separated from the loins of the disbelievers, Allah would have punished them with a painful punishment." [52]

Because it relates to His saying: ﴿We would have punished, when those who disbelieved put into their hearts zealotry - the zealotry of ignorance﴾, when they barred the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions from the House, and did not acknowledge ﴿In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾, nor the messengership of the Messenger of Allah. (The "hamiyyah", zealotry, is of the form fa'iliyyah, from the saying of the speaker: "Fulan protected his nose (hamiya anfahu), he protects with zealotry and protection." Al-Mutalammis said:

"Indeed I am among them, and my honour is their honour,
Just as the head protects its nose from being broken."

That is, it prevents. ﴿So Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and He made them adhere to the word of righteousness﴾, meaning sincerity. Its parallels are His saying: ﴿But it is piety from you that reaches Him﴾ [[Surat al-Hajj: 37.]] and His saying: ﴿Allah only accepts from the righteous﴾ [[Surat al-Ma'idah: 27.]].

We were informed by Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Shadhan al-Razi, in my reading to him, we were told by Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi al-Rabi' al-Qattan, we were told by 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hanbal, and Haytham - or Wahdam - ibn Hammam al-Amuli, and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd, they said: We were told by al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah, we were told by Sufyan ibn Habib, we were told by Shu'bah, from Yazid ibn Abi Najiyah, from al-Tufayl ibn Abi, from his father, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and He made them adhere to the word of righteousness﴾: "There is no god but Allah." [53] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/138; Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/63.]]

This is also the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, 'Amr ibn Maymun, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Salamah ibn Kuhayl, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, 'Ikrimah, Talhah ibn Musarrif, al-Rabi', al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: it is "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

We were informed by 'Abd al-Khaliq ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq, we were informed by Abu Bakr ibn Habib, we were told by Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Muzani, we were told by Abu Nu'aym and Abu Hudhayfah, who both said: we were told by Sufyan, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from 'Ayyash ibn Rabi'i, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning ﴿and He made them adhere to the word of righteousness﴾, that he said: "There is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest."

This is also the saying of Ibn 'Umar. 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: it is "There is no god but Allah alone, without partner, to Him belongs the dominion, to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things competent."

We were informed by Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun, we were informed by Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid, we were told by Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi in Nishapur, we were told by Salamah ibn Sulaym al-Sulami, we were told by 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, concerning ﴿and He made them adhere to the word of righteousness﴾, that he said: "In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful."

﴿And they were more worthy of it and deserving of it, and Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger Muhammad (peace be upon him) the vision that he saw concerning his departure to al-Hudaybiyah, that he and his companions would enter the Sacred Mosque. ﴿Certainly will Allah fulfil for His Messenger the vision in truth. You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in safety, with your heads shaved and hair shortened, not fearing.﴾ His saying "surely will enter" means: and he said "surely will enter", because the expression "the vision" is a statement. Ibn Kaysan said: His saying "surely will enter" is from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to his companions, relating his vision; so Allah the Exalted informed about His Messenger that he said that, and for this reason he made the exception out of courtesy with the courtesy of Allah the Exalted, when He said to him: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," except [with the qualification], "If Allah wills."﴾ [[Surat al-Kahf: 23.]] Abu 'Ubaydah said: "in" (in) means "when" (idh), its meaning being "when Allah wills," as in His saying: ﴿if you are believers﴾, and ﴿if they desire chastity﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 33.]].

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: It is permissible that the exception relates to the entering, because between the "vision" and its fulfilment there was a year, and some of them died during the year. So the meaning of the verse is: "You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, all of you, if Allah wills, in safety."

It is also permissible that the exception applies to the fear and the safety, not to the entering, because there was no doubt about the entering. For the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying when entering the graveyard: "And we, if Allah wills, will surely join you." [54] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/493, hadith 1547.]] So the exception applies to joining, not to death.

﴿So He knew what you did not know﴾, that the good lay in the treaty, which is His saying: ﴿And if not for believing men...﴾ [the verse]. ﴿And He gave, besides that, a near victory﴾, that is, besides their entering the Sacred Mosque and the fulfilment of the Messenger of Allah's vision. According to most exegetes, it is the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah. Al-Zuhri said: No conquest in Islam was greater than the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, because fighting had been where people met; but when the truce came, war was set aside, people were secure with one another, and they met and conversed and debated. No one who spoke with intelligence about Islam was not drawn into it in those two years, and more than had been in Islam before that.

Ibn Zayd said: It is the conquest of Khaybar, which Allah, exalted is He, granted them when they returned from al-Hudaybiyah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided it among all the people of al-Hudaybiyah except one man from the Ansar, namely Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah, who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyah but was absent from Khaybar.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (*al-Jawahir al-Hisan*) on surah 48, verses 22–27 (part 1 of 3):

﴿And if those who disbelieve fought you, they would surely turn their backs; then they would find neither a protector nor a helper.﴾ He means Asad, Ghatafan, and the people of Khaybar. Qatadah said: He means the disbelievers of Quraysh. ﴿The way of Allah, which has already passed before, and you will not find any change in the way of Allah.﴾ That is, like the way of Allah which has passed before, in granting victory to His friends and subduing His enemies. ﴿And He is the One who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the heart of Mecca,﴾ that is, al-Hudaybiyyah, ﴿after He had given you victory over them. And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do.﴾ (*al-Ya'*) Abu 'Amr and others read it with *ya'* (they), and others read it with *ta'* (you). They differed concerning who they were. Anas said: Eighty men from the people of Mecca descended upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions from the mountain of al-Tan'im at the time of the dawn prayer during the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, intending to kill them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took them alive and set them free. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And He is the One who withheld their hands from you…﴾ to the end of the verse.

'Ikrimah related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Quraysh had sent forty or fifty men from among them, and ordered them to circle around the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, to strike some of his companions, but they were seized. They were brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he pardoned them and released them. They had been pelting the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with stones and arrows. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And He is the One who withheld their hands from you…﴾ to the end of the verse.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughaffal said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) at al-Hudaybiyyah, beneath the root of a tree, and a branch of that tree was on his back. I lifted it from his back. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib was before him writing the treaty of peace, and Suhayl ibn 'Amr was there. Thirty young men came out to us armed, and they rushed at us. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) invoked Allah, and Allah blinded their sight. We stood up to them, seized them, and the Messenger of Allah released them. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse. [39] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/281.]]

Mujahid said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) came out intending to perform 'umrah, and his companions seized some people from the sanctuary who were unaware. The Prophet (ﷺ) released them. That is the "victory" in ﴿the heart of Mecca﴾.

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that a man among the companions of the Messenger of Allah, called Zunaym, looked out from the pass of al-Hudaybiyyah. The polytheists shot him with an arrow and killed him. The Messenger of Allah sent cavalry, and they brought twelve disbelieving horsemen. The Prophet of Allah said to them: "Do you have a covenant with me? Do you have a pact with me?" [40] They said: No. So he released them, and Allah revealed this verse.

Ibn Ayzi and al-Kalbi said: They were the people of al-Hudaybiyyah. When the Prophet (ﷺ) set out with the sacrificial animals and reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: "O Prophet of Allah, will you enter upon a people who are at war with you without weapons or horses?" He sent to Medina, and he left no horse or weapon there without taking it. When he approached Mecca, they prevented him from entering. He went on until he came to Mina, and he stayed at Mina. Then a spy came to him saying that 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl had come out against you with five hundred men. He said to Khalid ibn al-Walid: "O Khalid, this is your cousin who has come to you with horses." Khalid said: "I am the sword of Allah and the sword of His Messenger, O Messenger of Allah, send me wherever you wish." On that day he was named "the Sword of Allah." He sent him with cavalry, and he met 'Ikrimah in the ravine and defeated him until he drove him into the walls of Mecca. Then they returned a second time, and he defeated him until he drove him into the walls of Mecca. Then he returned a third time, and he defeated him until he drove him into the walls of Mecca. So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And He is the One who withheld their hands from you…﴾ to His saying ﴿a painful punishment﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) withheld from the remnants of the Muslims who had remained there after He had granted him victory over them, out of aversion that the horses might trample them without knowledge. [41] This is His saying: ﴿They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and the sacrificial animals detained from reaching their place of sacrifice.﴾ That is, they barred the sacrificial animals, held back. [42] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/123.]]

﴿from reaching their place of sacrifice﴾, that is, their place of slaughter. They were seventy camels.

Al-Zuhri related, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who both said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) left Medina in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, intending to visit the House, not intending fighting. He took with him seventy camels, and the people were seven hundred men, so each camel was for ten persons. When he reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, people joined him, and he set out with some hundreds of his companions. When they were at Dhu al-Hulayfah, he garlanded the sacrificial animals, marked them, and entered into the state of ihram for 'umrah. He sent ahead a spy from Khuza'ah to inform him about Quraysh.

The Prophet (ﷺ) continued until, when he was at the pool of al-Ashtat, near 'Usfan, the Khuza'i spy came to him and said: "I left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy and 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, who have gathered the Ahabish for you. They will fight you and bar you from the House." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Advise me. Do you think we should attack the offspring of those who assisted them and take them captive? If they remain seated, they will sit as men who have been wronged, and if they escape, it will be a neck which Allah has cut off. Or do you think we should head for the House, and whoever bars us from it, we will fight him?"

Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have not come to fight anyone, but whoever stands between us and the House, we will fight him." The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Then set out."

Abu Hurayrah used to say: I never saw anyone more consultative with his companions than the Prophet (ﷺ). They set out until, when they were at 'Usfan, Bishr ibn Sufyan al-Ka'bi met him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, these are Quraysh. They have heard of your journey, so they have come out with their nursing camels and their suckling young, wearing leopard skins. They have camped at Dhu Tuwa, swearing by Allah that you will never enter upon them. And this is Khalid ibn al-Walid with their horses, who have advanced them to Kura' al-Ghamim." I have mentioned the saying of one who said: On that day Khalid ibn al-Walid was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as a Muslim. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Woe to Quraysh! War has consumed them. What harm would it do them if they left me between myself and the rest of the Arabs? If they overcome me, that is what they wanted, and if Allah makes me victorious over them, they will enter Islam in multitudes, and if they do not do that, they will fight while still possessing strength. What does Quraysh think? By Allah, I will not cease to strive against them for the sake of what Allah has sent me with, until Allah makes it prevail, or my neck is severed." [43] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/323; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 20/16.]]

Then he said: "Who will lead us by a route other than the one they are on?" A man from Aslam said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." So he led them on a rough, difficult path between ravines. When they came out of it, the Muslims had found that burdensome, and it led to a level land at the end of the valley. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the people: "Say: We seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him." They did so, and he said: "By Allah, this is the 'hittah' (remission) that was presented to the Children of Israel, but they did not say it." [44] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/273; al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 4/189.]]

Then the Messenger of Allah said to the people: "Take the route to the right," along a path that leads out at the pass of al-Murar, descending upon al-Hudaybiyyah from the lower part of Mecca.

The army took that route. When the horsemen of Quraysh saw the departure of Quraysh (from its own route) and that the Messenger of Allah had diverged from their path, they spurred back to Quraysh to warn them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued until, when he took the pass of al-Murar, his she-camel knelt down with him. The people said: "Hal, hal!" He said: "What is 'hal'?" They said: "She has been made to stop, by force." He said: "She has not been made to stop, and that is not her habit, but the one who stopped the elephant has stopped her." [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/323; Sahih al-Bukhari: 3/178 with variation; Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/629.]] [45]

Then he said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, Quraysh will not ask me today for any arrangement by which they glorify the sacred things of Allah, and in which there is the maintenance of kinship, except that I will give it to them." Then he said to the people: "Dismount." They dismounted at the farthest part of al-Hudaybiyyah, at a well of little water, from which people could only take water in small amounts. The people soon exhausted it. The people complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of thirst. He drew an arrow from his quiver and gave it to a man of his companions called Najiyah ibn 'Umayr ibn Ya'mur ibn Darim, who was the driver of the sacrificial camels of the Messenger of Allah. He descended into that well and thrust it into its bottom, and the water gushed forth with abundance, until they departed from it. It is said that a girl from the Ansar came with her bucket, while Najiyah was in the well drawing water for the people, and she said:

"O you who draw water, my bucket is yours,
for I see the people praising you,
extolling your goodness and glorifying you;
I hope for good from you as they hope from you."

He said:

"The Yemeni girl knows
that I am the drawer, and my name is Najiyah.
And a stab that sprays weakly,
I stabbed it at the chests of the enemies."

He said: While they were thus, Budayl ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i came with a group from his people. Khuza'ah were the trusted confidants of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the people of Tihamah. He said: "I left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy and 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, who have camped at the farthest waters of al-Hudaybiyyah, with their nursing camels and suckling young. They will fight you and bar you from the House."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We have not come to fight anyone, but we have come as pilgrims performing 'umrah. Quraysh has been exhausted by war and has been harmed by it. If they wish, we will make a truce with them for a period, and they will leave me to deal with the people. If I prevail, then good; and if they wish to enter into what the people have entered into, they may do so. Otherwise, they will have gathered their strength. By Allah, I will fight them for this matter of mine until my neck is severed, or until Allah makes His command prevail." [46] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 9/219; al-Musannaf: 5/333 with variation; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 20/11.]]

Budayl said: We will convey to them what you say.

He set off until he came to Quraysh and said: "We have come to you from this man, and we heard him say a statement. If you wish, we will present it to you." Their foolish ones said: "We have no need for you to tell us anything from him." Those of their men with opinion said: "Say what you heard him say." He said: "I heard him say such and such." He related to them what the Prophet (ﷺ) had said.

Then 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi stood and said: "O people, are you not the father's offspring?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Am I not the offspring?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Do you suspect me?" They said: "No." He said: "Do you not know that I summoned the people of 'Ukaz, and when they insisted upon me, I came to you with my family, my children, and those who obeyed me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "This man has presented you with a path of right guidance, so accept it and let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." So he went to him and began speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet said to him something similar to what he had said to Budayl. 'Urwah then said: "O Muhammad, do you think that if you destroy your own people, you have heard of anyone among the Arabs who has pillaged (and it is said: uprooted) his own people before you? And if the other outcome occurs, by Allah, I see faces and rabble from the people who I think will flee and abandon you."

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Suck the clitoris of al-Lat!" (al-Lat was the idol of Thaqif, which they used to worship.) "Shall we flee and abandon him?" 'Urwah said: "Who is this?" They said: "Abu Bakr." He said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, were it not for a favour you had done me, which I have not repaid, I would have answered you." He kept speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ), and whenever he spoke, he took hold of his beard. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah was standing over the head of the Messenger of Allah, carrying a sword and wearing a helmet. Whenever 'Urwah reached out his hand toward the beard of the Prophet (ﷺ), he struck his hand with the scabbard of the sword and said: "Remove your hand from his beard!" 'Urwah raised his head and said: "Who is this?" They said: "Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah." He said: "You treacherous one! Am I not still striving to rectify your treachery?" Al-Mughirah had accompanied some people in the pre-Islamic era, killed them, and taken their property, then he came and embraced Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "As for Islam, we have accepted it. As for the wealth, it is wealth obtained by treachery, and we have no need of it." [47] [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/629; Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/275.]]

'Urwah began to glance at the companions of the Messenger of Allah with his eyes. He said: "By Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) will not spit out phlegm except that it falls into the palm of one of them, so he rubs it over his face and skin. When he commands them, they rush to carry out his command. When he performs ablution, they nearly fight over his ablution water. When they speak, they lower their voices in his presence, and they do not look at him directly out of reverence for him."

'Urwah returned to his companions and said: "O people, I have been received by kings. I have been received by Caesar, Kisra, and the Negus. By Allah, I have never seen a king whom his companions honour as the companions of Muhammad honour Muhammad. By Allah, if he spits out phlegm, it falls into the palm of one of them, so he rubs it over his face and skin. When he commands them, they rush to carry out his command. When he performs ablution, they nearly fight over his ablution water. When they speak, they lower their voices, and they do not look at him directly out of reverence for him. He has presented you with a path of right guidance, so accept it."

A man from Kinanah said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came in sight of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, the Prophet said: "This is so-and-so, from a people who honour the sacrificial camels, so send them to him." They were sent to him, and a group came to meet him reciting the talbiyah. When he saw that, he said: "Glory be to Allah! It is not right that these people be barred from the House." Then they sent to him al-Juls ibn 'Alqamah ibn Rayyan, who was then the chief of the Ahabish. When the Messenger of Allah saw him, he (ﷺ) said: "This man is from a people who venerate (the sacred), so send the sacrificial camels in front of him, so that he may see them." [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/324.]]

When he saw the sacrificial animals flowing toward him from the side of the valley, with their garlands, having worn down their pegs from being held back for so long, he returned to Quraysh without reaching the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), out of awe at what he had seen. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh, I have seen what must not be barred: the sacrificial animals with their garlands, having worn down their pegs from being held back for so long from their place of sacrifice." They said to him: "Sit down, for you are only a bedouin with no knowledge." Al-Juls grew angry at that and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah, we did not ally with you on this basis, nor did we make a pact with you on this basis, that you should bar from the House of Allah one who comes to it glorifying it. By the One in whose hand is the soul of al-Juls, either you will let Muhammad and what he came for go free, or I will break away with the Ahabish, breaking away as one man." They said to him: "Hold back from us, O Juls, until we take for ourselves what we are content with."

A man among them called Mikraz ibn Hafs stood and said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came in sight of them, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is Mikraz ibn Hafs, and he is a wicked man." He began speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ), when Suhayl ibn 'Amr came. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw him, he said: "Your affair has been made easy for you. The people come to you with their kinship ties, asking you for peace. So send the sacrificial animals and display the talbiyah, perhaps that will soften their hearts." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 10/478.]] They recited the talbiyah from the corners of the camp until their voices resounded with the talbiyah. Then they came and asked for peace. Suhayl said: "Come, let us write a document between us and you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, and said to him: "Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." Suhayl said: "As for 'al-Rahman' (the Most Merciful), I do not know what it is. But write: 'In Your name, O Allah,' as you used to write." The Muslims said: "By Allah, we will not write it except as: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to 'Ali: "Write: 'In Your name, O Allah,' " then he said: "Write: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed upon." Suhayl said: "By Allah, if we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have barred you from the House, nor would we have fought you. But write your name and the name of your father."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I am indeed the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me." Then he said to 'Ali: "Erase 'Messenger of Allah'." 'Ali said: "By Allah, I will never erase you, ever." So the Messenger of Allah took it, and he did not know how to write, so he erased it himself. Then he said: "Write: This is what Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah has agreed upon with Suhayl ibn 'Amr, and they have agreed to put down war among the people for ten years, during which the people will be safe and will restrain some from others, and on the condition that whoever comes to Mecca from the companions of Muhammad as a pilgrim, or performing 'umrah, or seeking the bounty of Allah, will be safe in his life and property; and whoever comes to Medina from Quraysh, passing through to Egypt or to Syria seeking the bounty of Allah, will be safe in his life and property; and on the condition that whoever comes to the Messenger of Allah from Quraysh without the permission of his guardian, he will be returned to them; and whoever comes from those with the Messenger of Allah to Quraysh, they will not return him to him."

Thereupon this was grievous to the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever comes to them from among us, may Allah keep him far away; and whoever comes to us from among them, we will return him to them. Allah knows best what is in the heart of anyone who has embraced Islam, and will make a way out for him. Between us is a closed chest (of trust), and there is no secret theft and no shackles. Whoever wishes to enter into the covenant and pact of Muhammad, may enter it; and whoever wishes to enter into the covenant and pact of Quraysh, may enter it." [48] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/325; al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/192.]]

So Khuza'ah sprang up and said: "We are within the covenant and pact of Muhammad." And Banu Bakr sprang up and said: "We are within the covenant and pact of Quraysh." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And on condition that they leave us free between us and the House, so that we may circumambulate it." Suhayl said: "The Arabs will not say that we were subdued by force. But this will be yours in the coming year." So he wrote: "And on condition that you turn back from us this year, and do not enter Makkah against us; and when next year comes, we will withdraw from it for you, and you may enter it with your companions and remain there three days, and enter it with no weapons except swords in their sheaths, and the arms of a rider. And on condition that this sacrificial animal is to be slaughtered wherever we are prevented from reaching it, and you shall not bring it forward against us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "We will drive it, and you will turn back its faces." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 10/480; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/125.]]

He said: While the Messenger of Allah was writing the document, he and Suhayl ibn 'Amr, there suddenly came Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn 'Amr, dragging his shackles, having escaped and come out from the lower part of Makkah until he threw himself among the Muslims. When Suhayl saw Abu Jandal, he stood up to him, struck his face, seized his chain, and said: "O Muhammad, the agreement between me and you has been concluded before this man came to you, and this is the first man I will hold you to it over. Will you return him to us?" Then he began to drag him to return him to Quraysh. Abu Jandal cried out at the top of his voice: "O company of Muslims, am I to be returned to the polytheists, when I have come as a Muslim? Do you not see what I have suffered?" He had been severely tortured for the sake of Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Jandal, be patient and seek your reward, for Allah will surely make a relief and a way out for you and for those with you among the oppressed. We have made a covenant between us and these people, and a treaty, and we have given them that on condition, and they have given us a pledge. We will not betray them." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/282.]]

'Umar ibn al-Khattab then leapt to Abu Jandal, walking beside him and saying: "Be patient, O Abu Jandal, for they are only polytheists, and the blood of one of them is the blood of a dog," and he brought the edge of the sword close to him. He said: 'Umar said: "I hoped he would take the sword and strike his father with it, but the man refused to harm his father."

They said: The companions of the Messenger of Allah had set out, not doubting the conquest, because of a dream the Messenger of Allah had seen. When they saw this, a great distress came upon the people, until they nearly perished, and the matter of Abu Jandal added evil to what they already suffered. 'Umar said: "By Allah, I have had no doubt since I embraced Islam until that day. So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Are you not the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?'"

He said: "I am the Messenger of Allah, and I do not disobey Him, and He is my helper." [49] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 20/14; Irwa' al-Ghalil: 1/58.]]

'Umar said: "Did you not tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Did I inform you that we would come to it this year?" I said: "No." He said: "Then you will come to it and circumambulate it." 'Umar said: "Then I came to Abu Bakr and said: 'Is this not truly the Prophet of Allah?'"

He said: "Yes." I said: "Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?" I said: "Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?" He said: "O man, he is the Messenger of Allah, and he does not disobey his Lord. Hold fast to his stirrup until you die, for by Allah he is upon the truth." I said: "Did he not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Did I inform you that you would come to it this year?" I said: "No." He said: "Then you will come to it and circumambulate it." 'Umar said: "I continued to fast, give charity, pray, and free slaves, because of what I did that day, fearing for the words I had spoken."

They said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had finished the document, he called upon men as witnesses to the treaty, from among the Muslims and from among the polytheists: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, 'Abd Allah ibn Suhayl ibn 'Amr, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Mahmud ibn Maslamah, brother of Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, Mikraz ibn Hafs ibn al-Ahnaf, who was a polytheist, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was the scribe of the document.

When the Messenger of Allah had finished his affair, he set out with the sacrificial animals, and the people set out. When the sacrificial animals reached a point short of the mountains that overlook the valley of al-Thaniyyah, the polytheists confronted them and turned their faces back. The Prophet (ﷺ) stopped where they had been held, which was al-Hudaybiyah, and said to his companions: "Stand up, slaughter, then shave your heads." He said: "By Allah, not one of them stood up."

He said this three times, and when none of them stood up, he went in and entered upon Umm Salamah, and told her what he had suffered from the people.

Umm Salamah said: "O Prophet of Allah, go out, and do not speak a word to any of them until you slaughter your camel and call your barber to shave you." So he went out and did not speak a word to any of them until he slaughtered his camel, and called his barber, who shaved him. The one who shaved him that day was Khirash ibn Umayyah ibn al-Fadl al-Khuza'i. On the day of al-Hudaybiyah, some men shaved and others cut short. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on those who shaved." They said: "And those who cut short, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "May Allah have mercy on those who shaved." They said: "And those who cut short, O Messenger of Allah?" 

They said: "Why did you single out those who shaved for mercy, rather than those who cut short?" He said: "Because they did not doubt." Ibn 'Umar said: "That was because the people had grown calm, and they said: 'Perhaps we will circumambulate the House.'"

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent, in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, among his sacrificial animals, a camel that belonged to Abu Jahl, with a silver ring in its nose, to enrage the polytheists by this. Then there came to him (ﷺ) believing women, and Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿O you who have believed, when there come to you the believing women emigrating...﴾ [[Surat al-Mumtahanah: 10.]] ... the verse. He said: So 'Umar divorced two wives he had who were in polytheism. He said: Then He forbade them to return them, and commanded that the dowries be returned at that time. A man said to al-Zuhri: "Was it because of the women?" He said: "Yes." So one of them was married by Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and the other by Safwan ibn Umayyah.

Then the Prophet (ﷺ) returned to Madinah. Abu Basir 'Utbah ibn Usayd ibn Harithah came to him, and he was a Muslim, and he had been among those who remained in Makkah. Azhar ibn 'Abd 'Awf and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi wrote concerning him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and sent a man from Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, with a mawla (freedman) of theirs, and they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with their letter, and said: "The covenant you made for us..." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Basir, we have given these people what you know, and it is not right for us in our religion to betray. Allah the Exalted will surely make a relief and a way out for you and for those with you among the oppressed." [50] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/283-284.]]

Then he handed him over to the two men, and they set out with him until, when they reached Dhu'l-Hulayfah, they stopped to eat dates they had. Abu Basir said to one of the two men: "By Allah, I see that your sword is fine." The other drew it, and said: "Indeed, by Allah, it is fine." He said: "Let me look at it." So he took it and struck the brother of Banu 'Amir with it until he killed him. The mawla fled, and went quickly until he came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), while he was sitting in the mosque. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw him approaching, he said: "This man has seen something frightening."

When he reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Woe to you, what is wrong with you?" He said: "Your companion has killed my companion." By Allah, he had hardly finished when Abu Basir arrived, girded with his sword, and stood before the Messenger of Allah, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have fulfilled your covenant, you handed me over to them, and - it was said: and returned me to them - then Allah rescued me from them." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Woe to his mother, he is a kindler of war. If only he had men with him."

When he heard that, he knew that he would return him to them.
